The distinctive presentation of SLO supports its clinical diagnosis. Medical treatment seems to support a favourable long-term outcome, despite the wide variation in protocols and doses. EFAs were commonly used as initial and maintenance therapy, and tetracyclines could often be excluded from the treatment protocol, thus complying with good antimicrobial stewardship practice.

papers.title: A Retrospective Comparison of Survival, Tumour Reduction and Relapse Outcomes Following Oclacitinib and CCNU Treatment in Dogs With Canine Epitheliotropic T-Cell Lymphoma.
papers.authors: Shen GB, Dehcheshmeh MM, Ebrahimie E, Knight E, Trott DJ, Shipstone M
papers.abstract: Canine epitheliotropic T-cell lymphoma (CETL) is an aggressive and generally incurable disease in dogs. CCNU (lomustine) is commonly used for management, even though it carries a significant risk of adverse effects. Several reports describe oclacitinib producing clinical improvement in affected dogs, yet comparative data between the two treatments are lacking. To compare the clinical outcomes in dogs with CETL treated with oclacitinib or CCNU, focussing on tumour reduction (response), survival time and time-to-relapse. This retrospective review (2008-2024) included 23 client-owned dogs with confirmed CETL treated with either CCNU (n = 11) or oclacitinib (n = 12). Outcomes included response (reduction in measurable tumour burden), survival (time from histopathological diagnosis to death) and time-to-relapse (for dogs with complete or good responses). Clinical presentation and adverse effects also were recorded. Additionally, sex, age and weight were compared between treatment groups to investigate potential confounding factors. No statistically significant differences were identified between oclacitinib and CCNU for response, survival or time-to-relapse (p > 0.05 for all). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival (log-rank test, p = 0.20). Oclacitinib was associated with fewer adverse effects and reduced monitoring intensity. These findings suggest oclacitinib may offer outcomes comparable to CCNU for CETL, with fewer adverse effects and less intensive monitoring. The small, retrospective sample limits firm conclusions, yet these results indicate that oclacitinib could be a reasonable, possibly safer palliative option warranting further prospective study.

papers.title: Clinical and Immunological Responses to Dermatophagoides farinae Allergen Immunotherapy in Dogs With Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Wannawong J, Tunhikorn M, Prangtaworn P, Saelim N, Srisai T, Indrawattana N, Sungpradit S, Tungtrongchitr A, Wiriyarat W
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) in dogs is a prevalent allergic disorder associated with environmental allergens, including the house dust mite Dermatophagoides farinae (Df). To describe clinical and immunological changes over time in dogs with canine (c)AD sensitised to Df undergoing Df allergen-specific immunotherapy (ASIT) and to test the hypothesis that ASIT is associated with changes in Canine Atopic Dermatitis Extent and Severity Index, 4th iteration (CADESI-04), pruritus and medication scores and selected immunological markers. Fifteen dogs with cAD sensitised to Df received ASIT for 12 months. Clinical evaluations included CADESI-04 and pruritus Visual Analog Scale (PVAS). Gene expression of interleukin (IL)-31, interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) was analysed using real-time PCR. Serum levels of Df-specific immunoglobulin (Ig)E, total IgG and IgG subclass 1 were measured using immunoassays. Evaluations were performed at 0, 6 and 12 months. Significant reductions in pruritus scores and IL-31 expression were observed, while IFN-γ expression increased. CADESI-04 scores decreased, although the change was not statistically significant. A reduction in medication scores was observed over time. Serum analysis showed increased concentrations of IgG and IgG1, while Df-specific IgE remained elevated. Dermatophagoides farinae ASIT resulted in a reduction in pruritus and medication use over a 12 month period. Associated with this, PBMCs IL-31 was reduced and IFN-γ elevated. An increased serum IgG and IgG1 were measured, and Df-specific IgE remained elevated. These findings support an immunological effect of ASIT, yet further studies with a larger cohort are required to validate the findings.

papers.title: A Novel Veterinary Molecular Multiplex Microarray Serological Allergen Test (Pet Allergy Xplorer; Nextmune) Versus Conventional Extract-Based Serological (Idexx; Stallergenes Greer Laboratories) Versus Intradermal Allergen Testing in 59 Dogs With Atopic Dermatitis: Evaluation of Agreement Between Allergy Testing Platforms.
papers.authors: Birchler D, Austel M, Banovic F
papers.abstract: The first veterinary multiplex molecular microarray serum allergy test (SAT), Pet Allergy Xplorer, is commercially available. However, no comparative evaluations of this test versus whole extract-based SAT (eSAT) platforms and intradermal allergen testing (IDAT) currently exist. Evaluate agreement between IDAT, conventional eSAT (Stallergenes Greer Laboratories) and extract and recombinant-containing SAT (erSAT) for shared environmental allergens in atopic dogs. Fifty-four dogs with non-seasonal (with or without seasonal exacerbation) and five dogs with seasonal atopic dermatitis were enrolled. IDAT, eSAT and erSAT were performed on the same day. Two independent investigators (Inv A and Inv B) recorded IDAT results. Per manufacturer guidance, 80 and 300 enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) absorbance units (eSAT80 and eSAT300) and 28 ng/mL (erSAT) were used as SAT cut-off values. Cohen's kappa (κ) and prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa (PABAK) were used to test agreement. Between IDAT investigators, there was almost perfect agreement across all allergens (κ = 0.81; PABAK = 0.87). Moderate agreement (κ = 0.58) between erSAT and eSAT300 across all allergens improved to almost perfect with PABAK (0.84). IDAT Inv A had the strongest agreement with eSAT300 (κ = 0.44, PABAK = 0.75) compared to erSAT (κ = 0.29, PABAK = 0.64) and eSAT80 (κ = 0.13, PABAK = 0.11); results were similar with Inv B. Agreement between testing platforms varied depending on the kappa statistic used, with low κ agreement for most comparisons, highlighting disagreements on what was considered positive. PABAK was generally higher, showcasing high overall concordance. Agreement to the new erSAT was strongest with eSAT300; agreement was moderate (κ) to almost perfect (PABAK).

papers.title: Rapid competitive ELISA incorporating Semliki Forest virus-expressed rabies virus glycoprotein for serological surveillance of canine and feline rabies immunity.
papers.authors: Han X, Sun S, Tian Y, Li L, Zhu X, Zhao J, Zhang Y, Zhou M, Zhang C, Zhao L
papers.abstract: Although the case fatality rate of rabies approaches 100%, it is entirely preventable through the use of vaccination-induced neutralizing antibodies. Rapid and reliable detection of these antibodies is therefore critical for effective disease control. Using a rabies virus glycoprotein expressed by Semliki Forest virus (SFV-RVG) as a coating antigen and horseradish peroxidase-labeled 7A3 (HRP-7A3) as the detection antibody, we developed a competitive ELISA (cELISA) for the specific detection of rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-neutralizing antibodies. On the basis of the testing of the in-house sample panel, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis revealed optimal cutoff values of 42.5% for canine serum and 54.5% for feline serum. The clinical agreement of the kit was excellent, with an overall percent agreement (OPA) of 95.67% for canine serum and 97.17% for feline serum. Overall, the cELISA reported here provides a promising tool for rabies immune surveillance in dogs and cats.

papers.title: Assessment of Clinical and Immunological Factors of Local Recurrence in Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
papers.authors: Mizuta K, Philibert H, Matsuyama A
papers.abstract: Canine soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) are locally invasive tumours, making local recurrence a major clinical challenge. Time to recurrence (TTR) and associated immune factors remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize the immune microenvironment of canine STS and identify factors associated with TTR. Medical records from 27 dogs with STS that recurred after surgery were reviewed. Histopathological, transcriptomic, and immunological analyses were performed in a tissue-available subcohort of 20 dogs. Immune-related gene expression was characterized using the NanoString canine IO panel. Tumour-infiltrating immune cells and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) were assessed immunohistochemically using CD3, CD20, and FoxP3. Associations with TTR were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models and log-rank tests. Median TTR was 358 days. Age and tumour location were associated with TTR in univariable analyses of the full cohort, but neither age nor the overall location effect remained significant when analysed together. Higher NOD2 expression and Cluster 1 assignment were associated with shorter TTR across exploratory multivariable models. Cluster 1 tumours exhibited abundant lymphocyte infiltration and enrichment of immunosuppressive pathways, whereas Cluster 2 tumours demonstrated lower immune infiltration and proinflammatory signatures. TLS-positive tumours had greater lymphocyte infiltration, with FoxP3+ cells accumulated within TLSs. Paired recurrent tumours contained significantly more large TLSs than primary tumours. Higher NOD2 expression and an immunologically active but suppressed tumour phenotype were associated with shorter TTR, whereas the association with anatomical location was model-dependent. Regulatory T cells and TLSs may contribute to the immune landscape associated with local recurrence and warrant further investigation as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Feline Mammary Carcinomas: Clinical Perspectives on Diagnosis, Staging, Treatment and Prognosis.
papers.authors: Petrucci GN, Lobo L, Queiroga FP
papers.abstract: Feline mammary carcinomas remain a major therapeutic and prognostic challenge in veterinary oncology because they combine high malignant potential, early dissemination, and substantial heterogeneity in clinicopathologic behaviour. This review summarizes current clinical knowledge on epidemiology, risk factors, diagnostic work-up, staging, treatment, and prognostic assessment of feline mammary carcinomas, highlighting areas of consensus and persistent controversies. Progress in care will require prospective, multicentre studies built on harmonized staging and pathology reporting, enabling risk-adapted treatment pathways that are both evidence-based and clinically actionable.

papers.title: Quality of Life Shapes Owner Decision-Making in Canine Cancer Care: Insights From Large-Scale Online Discourse.
papers.authors: Tarrant GA, Flory A, Rai TS, Wright A, Street TL, Wells K
papers.abstract: Canine cancer imposes substantial emotional, financial and decisional burden on owners navigating complex referral pathways and treatment options. Understanding how owners experience and interpret these pathways is essential to improving care delivery. We conducted a retrospective social media listening study using Pulsar Platform to retrieve public Anglophone posts relating to canine cancer across multiple platforms. After cleaning, de-duplication and zero-shot large language model relevance filtering (accuracy 88%-99%, F1 93%-98%, with precision up to 99% on Reddit), 11 878 posts were analyzed (of those that could be geolocated, most originated from the USA). Sentiment and emotion classification, thematic extraction and non-negative matrix factorization topic modelling were applied. Pre-specified subsets examined cost-focused (n = 2008), referral-focused (n = 341) and steroid-focused (n = 438) discourse. Overall, negative sentiment predominated (66%), with sadness the most frequent emotion (64%). Across platforms, quality of life (QoL) functioned as the primary decision-making framework, operationalized through appetite, mobility, comfort, engagement and "good days". Referral narratives highlighted delays, diagnostic sequencing uncertainty, travel burden and perceived gatekeeping within referral pathways. Financial constraint frequently shaped treatment feasibility, influencing decisions regarding chemotherapy, surgery, steroid-only palliation and euthanasia. Steroids were often described as a palliative bridge or cost-constrained alternative when advanced oncology care was inaccessible. General practise (GP) veterinarians were consistently referenced as trusted information anchors, influencing referral uptake and treatment trajectories. Topic modelling suggests a cancer-care pathway experienced as structurally constrained despite strong owner willingness to pursue treatment. QoL consistently supersedes cure as the dominant evaluative metric. Earlier cost transparency, clearer shared-care communication and strengthened GP-oncologist coordination may reduce decisional distress and help mitigate avoidable barriers to specialist care.

papers.title: Combination of Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy and Gilvetmab for the Treatment of Cutaneous or Subcutaneous Mast Cell Tumours in Dogs.
papers.authors: Martin TW, Thamm DH, Weishaar KM
papers.abstract: Gilvetmab is a caninised monoclonal antibody against canine PD-1. Concurrent or sequential administration of anti-PD-1 antibodies and radiation therapy (RT) improves survival time in various species. Eighteen dogs with mast cell tumours (MCTs) were prospectively treated with 24 Gy of RT over Days 0, 7 and 21 and gilvetmab every 2 weeks beginning on the second fraction of RT (Day 7) for up to 10 doses. Best tumour response was complete in one (6%), partial in eight (44%) and stable disease in nine dogs (50%) for an ORR of 50%. Median time to best response was 7 days after the first fraction of RT. Thirteen dogs (72%) developed progressive disease with a median progression free interval (PFI) of 116 days after the first fraction of RT. Nine adverse events (AEs) attributed to gilvetmab were recorded in seven dogs (39%) consisting of infusion reactions in four, metabolic changes in three and gastrointestinal signs and pancreatitis in one each. Overall, five dogs (28%) experienced Grade 3 AEs. Radiation AEs were limited to Grade 1 for both acute and late effects in seven dogs (39%). There was a significant difference in PFI and MST for dogs with and without lymph node metastasis with a median PFI of 64 versus 292 days and MST of 103 versus 587 days (p = 0.02 and 0.005, respectively). This sequence, or combination, of therapies did not provide durable tumour control for canine MCT and the AE profile warrants further evaluation.

papers.title: Plasma Dimethylarginine Concentrations in Dogs With Large Cell Lymphoma or Hemangiosarcoma: A Prospective Observational Study.
papers.authors: Marques GB, Maurey C, Le Roux D, Béguin J
papers.abstract: Asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) and symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) are endogenous methylated arginine derivatives associated with endothelial dysfunction and tumour progression in humans. Their relevance in canine oncology remains unclear. This prospective study aimed to assess plasma concentrations of ADMA and SDMA in dogs newly diagnosed with large cell lymphoma or non-cutaneous hemangiosarcoma (HSA); dogs with benign splenic lesions were also enrolled. Renal function was assessed at the time of inclusion to exclude overt kidney disease. Plasma ADMA and SDMA concentrations were measured at diagnosis, and clinical staging data were collected. A total of 31 dogs were enrolled: 11 with lymphoma, 15 with HSA and 5 with benign splenic lesions. SDMA concentrations exceeded the reference interval in 47%, 36% and 0% of dogs with HSA, lymphoma and benign lesions, respectively. Dogs with lymphoma (p = 0.003) and HSA (p = 0.013) had significantly higher SDMA concentrations than dogs with benign splenic lesions. Moreover, dogs with presumed disseminated HSA had significantly higher SDMA concentrations than those without metastatic disease (median: 21.5 vs. 12 μg/dL; p = 0.012). In contrast, plasma ADMA concentrations did not differ significantly among groups (p = 0.39). These findings suggest that lymphoma and HSA may represent extra-renal causes of SDMA elevation in dogs, and that SDMA could have value as a biomarker of tumour burden or progression. The potential clinical utility of ADMA in canine cancer warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Clinical Behaviour and Outcome of Pelvic Osteosarcoma in Dogs: A Retrospective Multicentre Analysis of 74 Cases (2007-2025).
papers.authors: Fejös C, Czichon F, Griffin M, Grillo N, Fournier Q, Oblak ML, Eng-Toogood M, Kent M, Desmas-Bazelle I, Kleiter M, Marconato L, McNaught K, Vincenti S, Chalfon C, Odatzoglou P, Rohrer Bley C
papers.abstract: Although osteosarcoma is the most common primary bone tumour in dogs, involvement of the pelvic bones is rare. The aim of the present study was to describe clinical presentation, identify possible prognostic factors, and evaluate outcomes in dogs diagnosed with pelvic osteosarcoma. Seventy-four dogs with cytologically or histologically diagnosed pelvic osteosarcoma were included in this multicentre retrospective study (2007-2025). The median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with comparisons performed using log-rank tests. Prognostic factors for PFS and OS were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Lameness (84%) was the most common presenting clinical sign, and the ilium (57%) was the most frequent intrapelvic tumour location. Thirty-one percent of dogs had metastases at diagnosis, primarily affecting the lungs. The median PFS was 75 days, and the median OS was 79 days. Dogs receiving any treatment had significantly longer PFS (116 vs. 7 days, p < 0.001) and OS (145 vs. 8 days, p < 0.001) than untreated dogs. No factors were significantly associated with PFS. In contrast, dogs with higher body weight and shorter time to diagnosis tended to have more favourable survival, whereas chemotherapy and local progression were associated with poorer outcomes. Despite the overall poor prognosis associated with pelvic osteosarcoma, treatment may extend survival. An individualized, often multimodal approach may provide clinical benefit in selected dogs.

papers.title: Toxicity of Cytarabine Intravenous Constant Rate Infusion in Cats With Lymphoma.
papers.authors: Hanford R, Skorupski KA, Rebhun RB, Brady RV, Al-Nadaf S, Lejeune AT
papers.abstract: Cytarabine intravenous constant rate infusion (IV CRI) toxicity in cats with lymphoma has not been well documented. We aimed to assess toxicities following cytarabine IV CRI as a single-agent or within a multiagent protocol in cats with lymphoma. Medical records of cats with lymphoma treated with cytarabine IV CRI, with documented dose, route, duration and at least one follow-up visit between 1990 and 2024, were retrospectively reviewed. Adverse events (AEs) were retrospectively graded according to VCOG-CTCAE v2. Thirty-eight cats were included, and 70 doses were evaluated for AEs. Median cytarabine dose was 389.8 mg/m 2 (range 100.1-697.3 mg/m 2 ) over a median infusion duration of 6 h (range 2-17 h). A total of 103 AEs were documented across 70 administrations. Gastrointestinal AEs were the most common category: altered appetite (21/38 cats, 55.2%), vomiting (9/38, 23.7%; one grade 3, the rest grades 1-2), diarrhoea (2/38, 5.3%) and dysphagia (2/38, 5.3%). Anaemia was the most common hematologic AE (14/38 cats, 36.8%; five grade 1, two grade 2, five grade 3, two grade 4); six cats (15.8%) developed thrombocytopenia (four grade 1, two grade 2), and one cat (2.6%) developed grade 2 neutropenia. Lethargy was the most common constitutional AE (12/38 cats, 31.6%). IV CRI of cytarabine was generally tolerated, with predominantly low-grade AEs, although grade 3-4 anaemia was not uncommon. Response rate and clinical benefit remain unknown; investigation of alternative dosing regimens may help clarify its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Immunohistochemical Characterisation of Mismatch Repair Proteins in Feline Cancers: A Pilot Study Using Validated Cross-Reactive Antibodies.
papers.authors: Nishibori S, Sakurai M, Kagawa Y, Nishigaki K, Nakagawa T, Inanaga S, Igase M, Mizuno T
papers.abstract: DNA mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is a clinically important biomarker in human oncology, yet its relevance in feline neoplasia remains poorly understood due to limited characterisation and the absence of validated reagents. In this study, we established a practical immunohistochemistry (IHC) approach for evaluating feline MMR proteins by confirming the cross-reactivity of anti-human MLH1, MSH2 and MSH6 antibodies using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered feline tumour cell lines lacking each target gene. Using these validated antibodies, we conducted a pilot screening to assess MMR protein expression in 83 feline tumours and observed variable reductions or losses of MLH1, MSH2 and MSH6 across several tumour types. Notably, MLH1 expression was lost in all melanoma cases (6/6, 100%) and in most osteosarcomas (14/15, 93%), indicating that MMR perturbations may be particularly relevant in these malignancies. These findings provide the first analytically validated framework for assessing MMR proteins in feline oncology and suggest that MMR dysregulation may be more widespread than previously recognised. Although the clinical sample size is limited, this initial pilot screening maps the preliminary landscape of feline MMR protein expression. Further large-scale validation studies incorporating microsatellite instability testing, methylation analysis and genomic profiling are warranted to clarify the biological significance of these alterations.

papers.title: Expression of Topoisomerase II Alpha in Canine Colorectal Polyps, Adenomas and Adenocarcinomas.
papers.authors: Fiedorowicz J, Paździor-Czapula K, Kołodziejski PA, Otrocka-Domagała I
papers.abstract: With the development and increased accessibility of diagnostic methods in veterinary medicine, the possibilities for early detection of proliferative lesions in the canine large intestine have expanded over the past decade. Since in human medicine, topoisomerase II alpha (Topo IIα) is considered a prognostic and predictive marker in various tumours, including colorectal carcinoma, we aimed to verify the role of this enzyme in proliferative epithelial lesions of the canine large intestine. In this study, we examined and compared the expression of Topo IIα in normal rectal mucosa, hyperplastic polyps, adenomas, and adenocarcinomas of the large intestine in dogs. Each type of lesion included 20 cases, in which the expression of Topo IIα was evaluated using immunohistochemistry. The median percentage of Topo IIα positive cells was 29.4% (IQR 24.9-37.1) in polyps, 30.3% (IQR 24.6-34.1) in adenomas, 36% (IQR 26.2-42.0) in adenocarcinomas, and 7.8% (IQR 5.9-10.6) in normal intestinal mucosa. Statistical analysis using the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn's post hoc tests with Bonferroni correction revealed significantly higher Topo IIα expression in hyperplastic polyps (p = 0.013, r = 0.62), adenomas (p = 0.033, r = 0.57) and adenocarcinomas (p = 0.002, r = 0.73) compared with normal rectal mucosa, with large effect sizes. Our results may serve as a preliminary basis for the potential use of anthracyclines in the treatment of canine colorectal adenocarcinomas, as well as in multiple adenomas or polyps when surgical options are limited. This study presents new insights of Topo IIα expression in canine large intestine carcinogenesis and could provide a valuable foundation for further clinical research.

papers.title: Canine Oral Melanoma as a Translational Model for Human Mucosal Melanoma: Molecular Architecture, Immune Landscape, and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.authors: Kuo CC, Chiu CL, Chung CS, Lin LS, Chen YM
papers.abstract: Human mucosal melanoma (hMM) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy with poor clinical outcomes and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapeutic strategies. Unlike cutaneous melanoma, hMM is characterized by an ultraviolet-independent pathogenesis, low tumour mutational burden, and pronounced molecular and immunological heterogeneity, which collectively inhibit effective translational modelling and therapeutic development. Naturally occurring canine oral melanoma (cOM) shares key biological features with hMM, including spontaneous tumour development in immunocompetent hosts, low mutational burden, extensive structural genomic alterations, and a highly immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. These shared characteristics support the positioning of cOM as a relevant comparative oncology model for investigating the mechanisms underlying tumour aggressiveness, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance in mucosal melanoma. In this review, we synthesize evidence suggesting that hMM and cOM are driven less by single dominant oncogenic mutations than by a complex convergence of pathway-level dysregulation arising from pervasive copy-number alterations, structural variants, and epigenetic plasticity. We further highlight the influence of these molecular features on immune visibility and immune suppression, as well as their contributions to the limited efficacy of single-agent targeted therapies and immune checkpoint blockade. Insights from canine immunotherapy studies provide preliminary translational support for combination-based therapeutic strategies and biomarker development. By integrating molecular, epigenetic, and immunological perspectives across species, this review supports the use of cOM as a comparative and translational platform for advancing therapeutic innovation in mucosal melanoma.

papers.title: Clinical Outcome and Histopathologic Assessment of Canine Perivulvar Mast Cell Tumours.
papers.authors: Ahrens MR, Corner SM, Masyr A
papers.abstract: Anatomic location is a known prognostic factor for canine mast cell tumours (MCTs). Previous publications have reported conflicting results about the clinical significance of MCT location in the inguinal and perineal regions and male genitalia. Hence, the goal of this study is to evaluate the grade, breed distribution and clinical outcome of canine perivulvar MCT. Surgical biopsy reports and associated medical records submitted between 2013 and 2024 to Michigan State University Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory were retrospectively evaluated. Information regarding age, reproductive status, breed, tumour location, microscopic description, histopathologic grade, and survival was collected. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate median survival time (MST) with dogs lost to follow-up (LTF) or alive censored from analysis. Biopsy reports from 64 dogs with 68 perivulvar MCT were evaluated. The most common phylogenetic classification was Mastiff-Terrier (47%). The majority (97%) of evaluated MCT were cutaneous, with 85% categorised as Kiupel low grade, while the remaining 15% were high grade. Three of 19 tumours (16%) that had c-KIT PCR performed had mutations in either Exon 8 or Exon 11. KIT expression pattern was classified as Pattern 2 or 3 in 71% of evaluated tumours. Median Ki-67 proliferation index and Ki-67 × AgNOR scores were 7 and 13, respectively. MST for the entire population was 868 days. Dogs LTF had a median follow-up time of 442 days. Dogs with perivulvar MCT may achieve prolonged survival time with surgical excision, and prospective studies are warranted to determine the effect of adjuvant therapy on outcome.

papers.title: Differential Effects of Cobalt Chloride Preconditioning on Vasculogenic Mimicry-Like Structure Formation in Two Canine Mammary Tumour Cell Lines.
papers.authors: Jeong Y, Ha JH, Chung JY, Choi JH, Ahn JO
papers.abstract: Vasculogenic mimicry (VM) is a tumour cell-lined vessel-like structure associated with poor prognosis, metastasis, and treatment resistance in human breast cancer. Furthermore, it has been described in canine mammary tumours (CMTs). Hypoxia is an established driving factor for VM formation in tumours with this capability. This study aimed to compare VM-like structure formation between two CMT carcinoma cell lines, CF41.Mg and CMT-U27. VM-like tubular structure formation was evaluated using a Matrigel-based 3D cell culture system under normal conditions and after CoCl 2 preconditioning. VM-like tubular structures were observed only in CF41.Mg cells, and CoCl 2 preconditioning increased the number of meshes and segments without a time-dependent difference between 24 and 48 h. In contrast, CMT-U27 cells did not form VM-like structures under the tested conditions. Subsequently, RNA sequencing, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and Western blot analyses were conducted. Exploratory RNA sequencing of untreated cells showed differences in the expression patterns of selected genes involved in angiogenesis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, cell migration, hypoxia-associated responses, and extracellular matrix organization between the two cell lines. CoCl 2 treatment was associated with VM-related transcriptional and protein-level changes in CF41.Mg cells. In contrast, CoCl 2 treatment was associated with E-cadherin upregulation and no significant changes in MMP2 or CDH2 expression in CMT-U27 cells. Taken together, under the tested conditions, CoCl 2 preconditioning enhanced VM-like structure formation in CF41.Mg cells but did not induce VM-like tubular structures in CMT-U27 cells.

papers.title: Fluvastatin Plus Dipyridamole Suppresses Canine Hemangiosarcoma Growth in Patient-Derived Xenograft Models Through Lactate Dehydrogenase-Associated Cholesterol/Lipid Metabolism.
papers.authors: Suzuki T, Tanaka S, Kishimoto K, Goto T, Yamazaki J, Kimura T, Aoshima K
papers.abstract: Tumour cells commonly exhibit aerobic glycolysis and produce lactate despite oxygen availability. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) catalyses pyruvate-lactate interconversion and regulates intracellular lactate levels. Endothelial cells also depend on glycolysis for ATP production, which prompted us to investigate LDH in canine hemangiosarcoma (HSA), a malignant endothelial tumour. We inhibited LDH with (R)-GNE-140 or sodium oxamate in two canine HSA cell lines (HU-HSA-2 and HU-HSA-3) and generated HU-HSA-3 clones with knockout of LDHA or LDHB to evaluate the effects of LDH perturbation. (R)-GNE-140 and sodium oxamate suppressed proliferation and reduced global histone lactylation levels in both cell lines. mRNA-sequencing (mRNA-seq) of (R)-GNE-140-treated HU-HSA-2 cells identified cholesterol/lipid metabolism-related gene sets among the top negatively enriched pathways. Representative cholesterol/lipid metabolism genes such as SREBF2, SQLE and LDLR responded differently depending on cell lines and inhibitors. (R)-GNE-140 decreased these genes in HU-HSA-2 but not HU-HSA-3, whereas sodium oxamate decreased them in HU-HSA-3 with limited effects in HU-HSA-2. In HU-HSA-3, LDHA and LDHB knockout clones decreased SREBP2 expression and reduced the number of lipid droplets. Fluvastatin, a cholesterol metabolism inhibitor, inhibited HSA cell growth in vitro but did not significantly suppress tumour growth in two HSA patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. In contrast, combined fluvastatin and dipyridamole treatment inhibited proliferation in vitro and tumour growth in PDX models. Collectively, these results suggest a context-dependent association between LDH and cholesterol/lipid metabolism in canine HSA cell lines and provide a rationale for further evaluation of combined cholesterol pathway inhibition.

papers.title: CT-Based Radiomic Features Predict Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis in Dogs With Oral Malignancy: A Machine Learning Study Using Leave-One-Patient-Out Cross-Validation.
papers.authors: Pinard CJ, Lagree A, Appleby R, Oblak M, Wu KC, Tran WT
papers.abstract: Accurate preoperative identification of cervical lymph node (LN) metastasis is essential for staging and treatment planning in dogs with oral malignancy, yet conventional imaging offers limited diagnostic sensitivity. This retrospective study evaluated whether CT-derived radiomic features, combined with machine learning classifiers, could predict the metastatic status of mandibular and retropharyngeal LNs. Forty-nine dogs with histopathologically confirmed oral malignancy underwent contrast-enhanced CT, and four bilateral cervical LN sites were manually segmented on images resampled to 1.0 mm isotropic spacing, yielding 195 LN observations (18 metastatic, 9.2%). One hundred and seven radiomic features were extracted per LN using PyRadiomics, and variance filtering, Spearman redundancy removal (|ρ| > 0.95), and Mann-Whitney U testing with Benjamini-Hochberg correction were performed within each fold of leave-one-patient-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to eliminate selection-leakage bias. Logistic regression, random forest (RF), support vector machine, and XGBoost were trained with SMOTE applied within training folds only, and two endpoints were evaluated on the same out-of-fold predictions: per-LN (primary) and per-patient (secondary, via maximum-probability aggregation across the four sites). Confidence intervals were derived from 5000-iteration patient-level bootstrap, and sensitivity analyses included repeated StratifiedGroupKFold cross-validation and cluster-robust generalised estimating equation (GEE) inference. At the per-LN level, RF achieved an AUC of 0.649 (95% CI 0.474-0.831; sensitivity 0.444, specificity 0.898) and XGBoost an AUC of 0.631 (0.501-0.772; sensitivity 0.944, specificity 0.379). Patient-level aggregation yielded an RF AUC of 0.613 (0.431-0.786; 9/13 metastatic-positive dogs identified) and an XGBoost AUC of 0.485. Four GLSZM/GLCM texture features were selected in 92%-100% of LOOCV folds and remained significant under GEE (adjusted p ≤ 0.012). CT-derived texture features therefore carry a reproducible, biologically interpretable signal for cervical LN metastasis, but leakage-controlled performance is modest in this proof-of-concept study, and external validation in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is required before clinical translation.

papers.title: Safety and Feasibility of Infusing Ex Vivo Expanded Allogeneic Canine Natural Killer Cells for the Treatment of Metastatic Solid Tumours.
papers.authors: Weisnicht AM, Szewc F, Cho MM, Cheng HH, Ganesh S, Mahoney L, Fox K, Smith PR, Olsen M, Richards RM, Vail DM, Capitini CM
papers.abstract: Companion canines need advances in therapeutic options for solid tumour malignancies. Natural killer (NK) cell infusions offer a promising treatment modality in canines with solid tumours. Autologous natural killer products are limited by dysfunctional immunity and a manufacturing process that delays care whereas allogeneic NK cells offer the possibility of 'off-the-shelf' therapy to be administered from healthy donors. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from healthy canine donors via density gradient separation. NK cells were expanded with recombinant human IL-2 and canine IL-21 with the addition of K562 feeder cells transfected with CD137 ligand and membrane bound human IL-15. Additional experiments included IL-12 during expansion. In vitro potency was assessed via co-culture with the D17-mKate2 canine osteosarcoma cell line. Three canines were enrolled in a phase 1 trial infusing ex vivo expanded allogeneic NK cells after lymphodepletion. Flow cytometric analysis confirmed successful expansion of canine NK cells with up to 50% of cells demonstrating NKp46+ after 14 days. Residual T cell numbers varied based on donor. The addition of IL-12 led to increased NK cell expansion. Incucyte demonstrated potency with increasing osteosarcoma cell death at higher effector to target ratios. Three canines with metastatic/refractory solid tumours were successfully lymphodepleted and infused with allogeneic NK cell products. The canines tolerated the infusions well. Canine allogeneic NK cells were successfully expanded and activated ex vivo, demonstrated potency in vitro and safety in vivo. Further studies will optimise the NK cell product and escalate dosing to reach the maximal tolerable dose.

papers.title: Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping Identifies Variable Cervical Drainage and Metastatic Nodes Outside Traditional Sampling Sites in Canine Oromaxillofacial Tumours.
papers.authors: Chrostek E, Lawrence J, Arzi B, Stewart N, Goldschmidt S
papers.abstract: Sentinel lymph node mapping (SLNM) has emerged as a key technique to guide decisions regarding nodal extirpation in dogs with oromaxillofacial tumours. The primary aims of this retrospective study were to describe the clinical utility of indirect computed tomographic lymphangiography (ICTL) for SLNM in a large cohort of dogs, characterise variability in SLN drainage patterns by tumour location, and describe the distribution of metastatic lymph nodes (LNs) identified by SLNM guided cytology or pathology. SLN locations, cytology, and available histopathology were reported as descriptive data. ICTL data were evaluated for 77 oromaxillofacial tumours in 74 dogs. A median of 2 SLNs were identified per ICTL dataset with 92% having at least one SLN identified. The ipsilateral mandibular lymphocentrum was the most common drainage basin; however, contralateral or bilateral drainage was frequent, occurring in over 55% of rostral tumours. Lateralized tumours were associated with a higher frequency of ipsilateral mandibular SLN identification compared with non-lateralized tumours (p = 0.0009). Of 68 dogs with malignant tumours, 10 (15%) had LN metastasis. Metastasis occurred in the SLN (n = 8), outside the SLN (n = 1), and in one dog without any identifiable SLNs. In 4 dogs (40%), metastasis extended beyond the ipsilateral lateral MLN; 3 dogs had metastasis exclusively in the medial retropharyngeal LNs. Among dogs with paired cytology and pathology, the false-negative rate of SLN cytology was 6.9%, potentially offering a low-morbidity screening method prior to LN extirpation. Future studies should seek to evaluate how SLNM with guided LN sampling influences patient outcomes, given its clinical feasibility.

papers.title: Comparison of Aerosolised and Traditional Tumour Margin Inking: A Prospective Blinded Histopathological Review in Canine Skin Tumours.
papers.authors: Wouters KL, Snelling SR, Morton JM, Stokes S
papers.abstract: Inking of canine skin tumours facilitates histopathological margin assessment. While traditional dab application is standard practice, aerosolised (spray) application may offer practical advantages. The objective of this study was to determine if aerosolised ink application provides comparable margin coverage to traditional dab methods and to compare time of application and volume of ink used. A blinded, randomised study on 19 canine skin tumours was performed. Each tumour was sectioned into two halves and one half randomly assigned a method (dab or spray) and ink colour (black or blue) with the other half receiving the alternative method and colour. Margin coverage (percentage of margin covered by ink), application time and ink volume were measured. Spray application was non-inferior to dab with respect to margin coverage, with mean margin coverage estimated as being 0.25 to 0.41 percentage points greater and lower limits of 95% confidence intervals -0.72 and -0.35 percentage points, respectively. Spray application was estimated as being 38 s faster on average (p < 0.001) but used approximately 0.5 mL more ink (p < 0.001). These findings suggest that aerosolised inking provides comparable margin coverage while reducing application time; however, ink placement fidelity was not assessed, and further evaluation is warranted to confirm full clinical equivalence.

papers.title: Surgery and Adjuvant Electrochemotherapy Compared to Surgery Alone for Treatment of Canine Incompletely Excised Soft Tissue Sarcomas.
papers.authors: Sofia R, Michael M, Gerry P, Joana GF, Lúcia LA, Patrícia DP, Andreia S
papers.abstract: The predominant challenge in canine soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) is achieving local tumour control, for which surgical excision remains the standard treatment. When complete margins are not attainable, adjuvant therapy may be recommended. Electrochemotherapy (ECT) combines cytotoxic drugs with electric pulses to enhance drug uptake and antitumour efficacy and has shown promising results. However, its role in incompletely excised STSs remains unclear, with limited control-group studies to confirm its efficacy. This retrospective study compared recurrence rate and time to recurrence (TTR) between dogs with incompletely excised cutaneous or subcutaneous low and intermediate-grade STSs treated with surgery alone or with adjuvant ECT and assessed ECT-related toxicity. Medical records from one oncology centre were reviewed. Dogs were included if completely staged, non-metastatic, and had a minimum follow-up of 10 months. The ECT protocol consisted of two sessions, 2 weeks apart, with intravenous bleomycin followed by biphasic pulses using plate electrodes. Forty-three dogs met the inclusion criteria: 22 underwent surgery alone, and 21 surgery followed by adjuvant ECT. Recurrence occurred in 68.2% and 33.3% of cases, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significantly longer TTR in the ECT group (median not reached vs. 534 days; p = 0.044). Treatment was well tolerated, with mild transient local inflammation in 38% of dogs. These findings support ECT as a safe and promising adjuvant therapy for improving local tumour control in incompletely excised canine STSs.

papers.title: Anti-Canine Mammary Carcinoma Effects of mPP-Based Nano-Micelles Encapsulating DPIA.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Wang H, Wang Z, Xie Y, Xu F, Liang X
papers.abstract: Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) presents a significant challenge in breast cancer treatment. Canine mammary carcinoma, characterized by spontaneous tumours in female dogs, serves as a robust spontaneous model for TNBC. In this study, DPIA, a potent antitumor agent, was encapsulated into synthesized mPEG-PCL (mPP) to form nano-micelles, aiming to enhance its in vivo therapeutic efficacy. DPIA@mPP exhibited more uniform dispersion and a spheroid-like architecture, with a drug loading rate of 4.31% and an encapsulation rate of 13.10%. Both DPIA@mPP and free DPIA exhibited comparable and significant cytotoxicity against canine mammary carcinoma cells (CMT-7364) in vitro. Encapsulation into mPP enhanced DPIA uptake by CMT-7364 cells, increasing tumour inhibition from 30.31% to 48.55%, while markedly reducing in vivo toxicity. Overall, the DPIA@mPP group demonstrated superior in vivo antitumor efficacy and a good safety profile. Furthermore, preliminary mechanistic studies suggest that DPIA@mPP may promote apoptosis in CMT-7364 cells, potentially through the inhibition of the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway, offering novel insights into TNBC treatment strategies.

papers.title: Long-Term Outcome of Electrochemotherapy in the Treatment of Advanced Stages (T 3 -T 4 ) of Feline Nasal Planum Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Franchini D, Laino I, Perrone C, Di Bello A, Ciccarelli S
papers.abstract: Electrochemotherapy is increasingly used as a locoregional treatment for feline squamous cell carcinoma, but its role in advanced nasal planum disease remains poorly defined. This retrospective study evaluated the long-term outcome of ECT as a sole treatment modality in 18 cats with T 3 -T 4 N 0 M 0 nasal planum squamous cell carcinoma. Adverse events were assessed according to VCOG-CTCAE v2. Response was assessed using RECIST v1.1 criteria, and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) and time to progression (TTP) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. At the end of treatment, 72.2% of cats achieved complete response, 16.7% partial response and 11.1% stable disease, resulting in an overall response rate of 88.8%. The 1-year complete response rate was 61.1%. Treatment response was significantly associated with PFS (p = 0.006), OS (p < 0.001) and TTP (p = 0.006), while recurrence was associated with shorter PFS (p = 0.003) and OS (p = 0.002). The 1-year risk of recurrence was 50%. Adverse events were mostly low-grade (VCOG Grade I-II) and self-limiting, the most common being transient local pain, erythema/crusting and pruritus; no grade ≥ 3 complications such as tissue necrosis or fistula formation were observed. These results suggest that ECT is an effective and well-tolerated treatment also in advanced stages nasal planum squamous cell carcinoma, with high response rates and long-term control disease. The risk of recurrence underscores the need for prolonged follow-up, as additional treatment sessions may be performed upon relapse, while ECT can also be used with palliative intent to prolong survival while preserving quality of life.

papers.title: Chronic Recurrent Septic Peritonitis in a Diabetic Dog Caused by Staphylococcus pseudintermedius With Splendore-Hoeppli Reaction (Botryomycosis-Like/Bacterial Pseudomycetoma).
papers.authors: Taylor D, Granger KL, Cohen A
papers.abstract: A 6-year-old neutered male Miniature Pinscher with poorly regulated diabetes mellitus was evaluated for recurrent abdominal effusion, lethargy and inappetence secondary to chronic septic peritonitis. Across four discrete clinical episodes, Staphylococcus pseudintermedius was repeatedly isolated in pure culture from peritoneal fluid and omental tissue, with consistent antimicrobial susceptibility profiles across submissions, a pattern suggestive of strain persistence rather than serial reinfection. Histopathology of omental biopsies demonstrated severe, chronic pyogranulomatous peritonitis with prominent Splendore-Hoeppli material surrounding bacterial colonies, consistent with bacterial pseudomycetoma. Despite two exploratory laparotomies with extensive abdominal lavage, closed-suction peritoneal drainage, broad-spectrum systemic antimicrobial therapy, and a subsequent salvage protocol of combined intravenous and intraperitoneal meropenem administered via an ultrasound-guided peritoneal catheter, infection ultimately recurred and the dog was humanely euthanized. The case is consistent with biofilm-associated chronic infection compounded by immune-complex deposition and concurrent endocrine disease, and supports consideration of regional antimicrobial delivery as a salvage strategy in refractory septic peritonitis when source control and systemic therapy alone prove insufficient.

papers.title: Molecular Detection and Characterization of Cryptosporidium spp. and Giardia duodenalis in Domestic Animals and Wildlife in Thailand With a Focus on Zoonotic Potential.
papers.authors: Udonsom R, Nishikawa Y, Mahittikorn A, Prasertbun R, Mori H, Ngaosuwankul N, Pintong AR, Jirapattharasate C, Stensvold CR, Popruk S
papers.abstract: Cryptosporidium spp. and Giardia duodenalis are important parasitic protozoa infecting humans and a wide range of animal species. Some species and assemblages have zoonotic potential and pose health risks to both humans and animals. This study aimed to molecularly detect and characterize Cryptosporidium spp. and G. duodenalis and assess their zoonotic potential in pigs, cattle, cats and wildlife. Nested PCR and sequence analyses of the small subunit ribosomal RNA (ssu rRNA) gene for Cryptosporidium spp. and ssu rRNA, β-giardin (bg), glutamate dehydrogenase (gdh) and triosephosphate isomerase (tpi) genes for G. duodenalis were used for molecular detection and characterization. The PCR positivity rate for Cryptosporidium was 17.9% (12/67) in pigs, whereas the corresponding rates for G. duodenalis were 6.0% (4/67) in pigs and 2.5% (2/80) in cats. Neither parasite was detected in cattle (0/61) or wildlife (0/144). Cryptosporidium scrofarum, a potentially zoonotic species, was the only Cryptosporidium species identified. Among the four Giardia-positive pig samples, assemblages B and E were each identified in two samples. Co-infection with C. scrofarum and assemblage E was detected in one pig. Feline-associated assemblage F was identified in two cat samples. Potentially zoonotic C. scrofarum and zoonotic G. duodenalis assemblage B were detected in pigs, together with livestock-associated assemblage E. Feline-associated assemblage F was identified in cats. These findings provide historical, sample-specific molecular data on the animals examined.

papers.title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
papers.authors: Demeyere M, Dufourni A, Verhaeghe LM, Paulussen E, Heirman L, De Baere S, Croubels S, De Backer T, van Loon G, Decloedt A
papers.abstract: Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses. To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR. Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe). Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests. Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected. Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity. Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR. This study investigated four biomarkers in the blood of horses with and without mitral valve regurgitation (MR), a condition in which the heart’s mitral valve does not close completely and allows blood to leak backwards. We also examined whether these biomarkers were related to billowing of the mitral valve, where part of the valve bulges backwards during contraction of the heart. The main findings were: Horses with MR had lower blood levels of ionized magnesium (iMg) than horses without MR.Horses with MR showed more pronounced billowing of the mitral valve.Valve billowing was greater in horses in which the backward flow of blood increased towards the end of contraction of the heart. However, lower iMg levels were not related to the degree of valve billowing. In addition, the other three biomarkers studied (5-HT, NT-proBNP, and cTnI) did not show meaningful differences between horses with and without MR.

papers.title: Squamous cell carcinoma involving the anal sac region in a cat: clinical course and multimodal management with toceranib and electrochemotherapy.
papers.authors: C P, D F, I L, M A C, A DB, S C
papers.abstract: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is one of the most common malignant epithelial tumours in cats, typically arising in the oral cavity or at cutaneous sites, whereas involvement of the anal sac region is exceptionally rare, with only two cases previously reported. An 8-year-old neutered male Domestic Shorthair cat was referred for persistent tenesmus, constipation and anorexia. A perianal swelling had initially been interpreted as anal sacculitis on cytology, but incisional biopsies confirmed SCC, characterised histologically by only moderate atypia and a low mitotic count. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a non-circumferential mass centred on the left anal sac region with infiltration of the perirectal soft tissues causing partial rectal obstruction, together with regional lymphadenomegaly; nodal metastasis was confirmed cytologically. Surgery and radiation therapy were declined, and palliative treatment with toceranib phosphate and meloxicam was started. After approximately one month of clinically stable disease, one session of electrochemotherapy with intravenous bleomycin was performed. Clinical signs transiently improved, but rapid progression occurred shortly thereafter, with invasion of the pelvic urethra. The cat died 68 days after diagnosis. Despite reassuring histological features, the tumour showed aggressive local behaviour and early regional metastasis. Toceranib was associated with transient clinical improvement and electrochemotherapy produced only short-lived improvement, likely because the lesion's extent and depth precluded complete treatment of the tumour volume. This case documents aggressive behaviour in an SCC involving the anal sac region and supports considering SCC in cats with persistent perianal swelling, tenesmus or defecatory difficulty unresponsive to medical treatment.

papers.title: Short- and long-term effects of dapagliflozin as an adjunct to insulin therapy in diabetic dogs: a pilot study.
papers.authors: Nogueira TB, Lopes JLX, Soares FAC, da Silva DI, Gusmão CB, Teixeira GG, Pöppl ÁG
papers.abstract: This study evaluated adjunctive dapagliflozin therapy in insulin-treated diabetic dogs to assess short- and long-term glycemic, clinical, and laboratory outcomes in dogs with naturally occurring diabetes mellitus. Six diabetic dogs received a compounded liquid oral dapagliflozin (CLODapa) formulation (0.088 ± 0.013 mg/kg once daily) in addition to ongoing insulin therapy for 100 days. We monitored continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) before and after treatment initiation, and serially assessed clinical, biochemical, and urinary parameters. Short-term dapagliflozin administration significantly reduced mean interstitial glucose, glucose nadir and peak values, and increased time within the target glucose range (60-250 mg/dL), while decreasing time above range. Glycemic variability increased, although time spent < 60 mg/dL and clinical hypoglycemia did not increase; however, CLODapa's initial dosage was reduced in four dogs due to concerns about hypoglycemia, increased in one, and left unchanged in another. Long-term treatment was associated with reductions in fructosamine, systolic blood pressure, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and cholesterol concentrations. No evidence of diabetic ketoacidosis, urinary tract infection, electrolyte imbalance, or acid-base disturbance was detected. Unintentional weight loss was documented in three patients and required a ~ 25% increase in food intake. Adjunctive dapagliflozin showed promise in improving glycemic control in diabetic dogs despite posing a risk of hypoglycemia, supporting further investigation of SGLT2 inhibition in canine diabetology.

papers.title: Heat-inactivated Bifidobacterium adolescentis LA20 alleviates doxorubicin-induced senescence and barrier dysfunction in feline intestinal epithelial cells.
papers.authors: Wang H, Liu T, Bai H, Jin H, Li Y, Wang Z
papers.abstract: To investigate the protective effects and molecular mechanisms of heat-inactivated Bifidobacterium adolescentis LA-20 (HT-LA20) against doxorubicin (DOX)-induced senescent injury in feline intestinal epithelial cells (FIECs). This in vitro experimental study was conducted from November 1, 2025, through August 31, 2026, and involved only FIECs. No clinical patients or animals were included. The DOX-induced injury and senescence model was established in FIECs. The effects of HT-LA20 on cellular senescence and related proteins were evaluated by senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining, cell viability assays, and ELISA. Transcriptomic sequencing and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to elucidate the molecular regulatory mechanisms. Cell-based assays and transcriptomic and untargeted metabolomic analyses were performed with 4 independent biological replicates/group. HT-LA20 reversed DOX-induced reductions in cell viability and cellular senescence; upregulated tight junction proteins and mucins 1 and 2; suppressed release of IL-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α, IL-8, monocyte chemoattractant protein 1, and matrix metalloproteinase 1; and promoted VEGF and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) secretion. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses showed that HT-LA20 reversed DOX-induced omic disturbances. Integrated multiomics Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis indicated that its effects centered on the retinol metabolism-serotonergic synapse-intestinal immunoglobulin A immune network multitarget axis and regulation of inflammatory pathways, including nuclear factor κ B and Toll-like receptor signaling. HT-LA20 effectively alleviates DOX-induced injury in FIECs by restoring intestinal epithelial barrier function and suppressing inflammatory senescence. These findings provide a theoretical basis for subsequent in vivo studies on postbiotics for chemotherapy-induced intestinal injury in veterinary medicine; clinical application requires further validation.

papers.title: Advanced heartworm disease in dogs is associated with marked right heart and pulmonary artery remodeling.
papers.authors: Kim M, Seo MW, Cho J, Park C
papers.abstract: To characterize echocardiographic findings of right heart and pulmonary artery remodeling in dogs with heartworm disease. Medical records were searched for those of client-owned dogs with heartworm infection diagnosed from July 2020 through February 2023 and with no major systemic diseases not attributable to heartworm infection. Results for variables of interest were compared for dogs grouped by heartworm clinical class (classes 1 and 2 [mild] vs classes 3 and 4 [advanced]), pulmonary hypertension probability (low and intermediate vs high), and tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (mild, moderate, or severe). Pre- and postextraction variables were also compared for dogs with caval syndrome. 44 dogs were included. Compared with dogs with mild heartworm disease (n = 23), dogs with advanced heartworm disease (21) had greater right atrial and right ventricular enlargement, less right pulmonary artery distensibility, shorter pulmonary artery acceleration time, higher main pulmonary artery-to-aorta ratio, and lower right ventricular systolic function. Similar results were identified for dogs with high (vs intermediate or low) pulmonary hypertension probability. Normalized right atrial diameter had the highest discriminatory performance for identifying advanced heartworm disease (area under the curve, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88 to 1.00), followed by tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient, normalized right ventricular dimension, and other variables. Right atrial size significantly decreased after heartworm extraction (n = 8 dogs). Advanced heartworm disease is associated with marked right heart and pulmonary artery remodeling. Echocardiographic assessment of right heart remodeling may assist clinicians in evaluating heartworm disease severity and identifying dogs with clinically important cardiopulmonary involvement.

papers.title: Chemodectoma Arising From the Abdominal Aorta in a 9-Year-Old Female Dog: Clinical, Histopathological and Immunohistochemstric Study.
papers.authors: Boskabadi SA, Nikroo KS, Mirshahi A, Nourani H, Hadiyan SS
papers.abstract: Chemodectomas are uncommon, typically benign neoplasms derived from paraganglionic chemoreceptor tissues, most frequently arising in the heart base or carotid bodies of brachycephalic dogs. This report documents a detailed pathological description of a chemodectoma originating from the abdominal aorta in a non-human species, representing, to our knowledge, the first case specifically characterized by its origin at the aortic trifurcation, thereby expanding the recognized anatomical spectrum of this tumour entity. A 9-year-old spayed female terrier was presented with persistent panting, recent-onset obesity following previous cachexia, and a complex clinical history including polyuria/polydipsia and pyoderma. Haematological and biochemical analyses revealed a regenerative anaemia, leucocytosis, and biochemical indicators suggestive of cholestasis and potential endocrinopathy. Advanced imaging identified a solitary, well-demarcated, highly vascular abdominal mass closely associated with the aortic trifurcation. Given the tumour's inaccessibility and pronounced vascularity, cytological confirmation via fine needle aspiration was precluded due to haemorrhagic risk, necessitating exploratory laparotomy. Intraoperatively, the mass was unresectable because of its anatomical relationships and the prohibitive risk of catastrophic haemorrhage. Humane euthanasia was subsequently elected. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated a lobulated neoplasm composed of pleomorphic neuroendocrine cells, with low mitotic activity and an absence of necrosis or haemorrhage. Immunohistochemistry confirmed strong, diffuse synaptophysin reactivity and focal neuron-specific enolase positivity, while chromogranin A and S100 protein were negative, underscoring immunophenotypic variability. This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity and therapeutic limitations posed by extra-cardiac chemodectomas in veterinary species, especially when located in unconventional anatomical sites. Limitations included the unavailability of computed tomography and lack of postoperative follow-up. This report expands the recognized clinico-pathological spectrum of chemodectomas and highlights the necessity for multidisciplinary diagnostic strategies and further research aimed at defining optimal management protocols for such rare and challenging presentations.

papers.title: Determination of reference intervals for symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) in Lacaune sheep.
papers.authors: Kiene F, Wagener MG, Röhrig P, Ganter M
papers.abstract: Traditional biomarkers such as serum creatinine and urea often fail to reflect early renal dysfunction, particularly in emaciated animals, as they depend on muscle mass or dietary protein intake. Symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA), a novel renal biomarker, has shown promise in other species for earlier and more sensitive detection of kidney disease. However, reference intervals for SDMA in ovine species remain undocumented. This study aimed to establish reference intervals for serum SDMA in clinically healthy Lacaune sheep. A reference population of 143 healthy sheep, stratified by age (juvenile < 1 year, adult ≥ 1 year), was selected based on clinical health, body condition score, and serum creatinine concentration. Serum SDMA was quantified using an ELISA validated for cats and dogs. Reference intervals were calculated as 0.59-1.72 µmol/l for all sheep, 0.59-1.56 µmol/l for adults, and 0.59-1.83 µmol/l for juveniles, with juveniles exhibiting significantly higher concentrations (p < 0.001). No sex-related differences were observed. In a retrospective analysis of 51 deceased sheep with histopathological renal assessments, SDMA concentrations were significantly elevated in animals with severe renal lesions compared to those with no, mild or moderate lesions (p = 0.005). Creatinine by contrast did not show significant differences. Notably, in animals with poor body condition, SDMA remained effective in identifying individuals with severe renal lesions, whereas creatinine levels remained within or below the reference interval. These findings suggest that SDMA is a more sensitive indicator of renal dysfunction in sheep than creatinine, particularly in emaciated individuals. The established reference intervals provide a foundation for clinical application. The economic feasibility of SDMA testing remains a limitation, but its potential to improve early diagnosis of renal disease in sheep justifies further investigation.

papers.title: Genomic analysis of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with a severe episode of self-trauma and urinary tract infection.
papers.authors: Repossi CP, Paiva SC, Simões MN, Fernandes BM, Silva JVO, de Araújo TA, Ferraz CM, Senhorello ILS, Rossi GAM, Furlan JPR
papers.abstract: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales are emerging pathogens of major importance in veterinary medicine. This study describes the clinical, microbiological, and genomic characteristics of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with paraparesis and concurrent pyelonephritis, chronic cystitis, and a self-traumatized limb lesion. A 12-year-old mixed-breed female dog underwent repeated antimicrobial therapy during hospitalization. Urine obtained by cystocentesis and wound samples were cultured, and ESBL-producing strains were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequence-based analysis. CTX-M-55-producing E. coli sequence type (ST) 457, phylogroup F, O11:H25, and fimH145, was recovered from urine and wound samples, while the wound sample also yielded a CTX-M-15- and SHV-2-producing K. pneumoniae ST39, KL149:OL2α.2. The two closely related E. coli strains differed by 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms, despite sharing the same ST, resistome, plasmid replicons, and virulence profile. ESBL-positive strains carried multiple virulence genes, with the E. coli strains classified as extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli strains. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae ST39 in an animal in Brazil. The co-occurrence of ESBL-producing E. coli ST457 and K. pneumoniae ST39 in the same dog highlights the potential for companion animals to harbor clinically relevant multidrug-resistant lineages and reinforces the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship in this sector.

papers.title: Dietary taurine mitigates waterborne arsenic trioxide toxicity in Nile tilapia: effects on growth performance, intestinal health, stress biomarkers, and immune-related genes.
papers.authors: Radwan M, Ragab AM, Bashar MAE, Al Malki JS, Al-Megrin WAI, Moussa MA
papers.abstract: Chronic arsenic contamination can compromise fish performance and health, yet practical nutritional approaches to limit its effects remain poorly defined. This 60-day study tested whether dietary taurine (TA; 10 g kg⁻¹ diet) mitigates waterborne arsenic trioxide (As₂O₃; AS; 10 µg L⁻¹, nominal) toxicity in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) using a 2 × 2 factorial design (with or without AS and TA; four aquaria per treatment, 15 fish per aquarium). AS exposure significantly reduced growth, feed efficiency, digestive enzyme activities, intestinal health, blood indices, innate immunity, and antioxidant responses, while increasing markers of hepatorenal stress, lipid peroxidation, intestinal injury, tissue DNA fragmentation, and IL-1β, HSP70, and Casp3 gene expression (P < 0.05). Observed survival was 70.00% in the AS group compared with 98.33% in the control group. In AS-exposed fish, TA improved growth and feed conversion, preserved villus architecture, restored most haematological, biochemical, immune, and antioxidant variables, enhanced SOD, CAT, GPx, and Nrf2 transcript abundance, and lowered MDA, DNA fragmentation, and inflammatory, stress, and apoptotic gene expression. Most responses in the AS + TA group approached control values. Significant AS × TA interactions for most statistically analysed variables indicated that TA conferred marked benefits during the AS challenge. In conclusion, dietary TA improved the physiological resilience of Nile tilapia to chronic exposure to waterborne As₂O₃ by supporting intestinal function and redox-immune balance.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides for companion animals: research advances, translational challenges, and opportunities.
papers.authors: Pan S, Wei Y, Sun M, Yu H, He P, Zhang G, Qiao S, Wu Y, Yang Q
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a growing global threat to public health, necessitating the development of novel antimicrobial strategies. Companion animals, particularly dogs and cats, are increasingly integrated into human lives, and their close interactions with humans facilitate the transmission of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Therefore, the use of contemporary antimicrobials in these animals raises significant concerns for both animal and human health. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), a class of naturally occurring peptides, play a critical role in host innate immunity through dual antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activities. Due to their pleiotropic mechanisms of action and lower selective pressure for resistance, AMPs are emerging as promising alternative candidates to conventional antimicrobials. Notably, accumulating evidence has also highlighted the promising antitumor capacity of AMPs, expanding their therapeutic potential beyond microbial infection control. Despite their potential, research on AMPs in companion animals remains limited, with most available evidence derived from in vitro assays and pre‑clinical in vivo experiments, while well‑controlled clinical studies are sparse. This review overviews recent advances in AMP research in dogs and cats, discusses major challenges in their development, and outlines future directions for their application in veterinary medicine. The adoption of AMPs in small animal practice has the potential to improve animal health while contributing to the mitigation of AMR. Collectively, this review offers new insights into the development of multifunctional novel therapeutic strategies in companion animals.

papers.title: Survival time and prognostic factors in cats with suspected acute pyelonephritis.
papers.authors: Fletcher JR, Gal A, Dill-Macky E, Cook EK, Harris LM, Mackie JT, Malikides N
papers.abstract: Although acute pyelonephritis (APN) is considered to have a better prognosis than other causes of acute kidney injury (AKI) in cats, survival time and prognostic factors are poorly defined. To determine survival time and prognostic factors influencing survival time in cats suspected of APN. Fifty-four client-owned cats with suspected APN. A retrospective cohort study was designed to review medical records between June 2017 and December 2025 for clinical data and survival time. Overall survival time was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox proportional hazard regression univariable screening then multivariable modeling identified factors associated with survival. Clinical features of survivors and non-survivors to 30-days after presentation were compared. Median survival time (MST) was 390 days (95% CI, 153-774 days). Cats that experienced less than 50% reduction or any increase in percentage change in serum creatinine concentration between hospital admission and discharge or euthanasia (sCrΔ%) had significantly higher hazards of death than cats experiencing greater than 50% reduction in sCrΔ%, after adjusting for International Renal Interest Society (IRIS) AKI grade and admission temperature (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 8.4 × 104-1.1 × 106; 95% CIs, 4.9 × 102-3.1 × 108; P < .001). No other factors, including pre-existing chronic kidney disease, infecting bacterial isolate, or antimicrobial regimen used, were independently associated with overall survival time. Cats suspected of APN have favorable long-term prognosis. Less reduction or any increase in sCrΔ% was associated with shorter survival time, with the prognostic effect strongly influenced by IRIS AKI grade and temperature at admission. Acute pyelonephritis (APN), a bacterial infection of the kidneys, is an important cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) in cats. Although APN is generally considered to have a better prognosis than other causes of AKI, the prognosis and factors associated with survival time in cats are poorly defined. This study followed 54 cats with suspected APN to evaluate survival time and factors associated with survival time. MST was 390 days, although individual survival times varied. Cats whose kidney function improved less or worsened during hospitalization had shorter survival times than cats with a greater improvement in kidney function. The severity of AKI and body temperature at admission influenced this association. In contrast, pre-existing chronic kidney disease, type of bacteria implicated in the infection, and the antimicrobial treatment used were not independently associated with survival time. Therefore, less improvement in kidney function, higher AKI grade, and decreased body temperature during hospitalization together indicate a less favorable prognosis in cats suspected of APN and may offer pet owners a stronger decision-making foundation.

papers.title: Elimination kinetics of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during carbon hemoperfusion in 19 dogs with toxicosis.
papers.authors: Her J, Labato MA, Langston CE, Butty EM
papers.abstract: To describe the elimination kinetics of NSAIDs during carbon hemoperfusion (cHP) in dogs with toxicosis, specifically the apparent elimination rate constant, half-life, and plasma reduction. 19 client-owned dogs (median age, 2.5 years; median body weight, 22 kg) with ibuprofen (n = 10), carprofen (5), or naproxen (4) toxicosis treated with cHP at 2 academic veterinary teaching hospitals from November 30, 2022, through July 7, 2024. Dogs were presented after known or suspected ingestion at median estimated maximum doses of 720, 200, and 325 mg/kg for ibuprofen, carprofen, and naproxen, respectively. The median interval from ingestion to cHP was 6.8 hours. Plasma concentrations were measured by LC-MS-MS in-serial samples collected during and, when available, after cHP. The median total plasma reduction was 58% (IQR, 51 to 80). The overall half-life during cHP was 1.3 hours (IQR, 1.1 to 1.8) by the 2-point method, concordant by regression (1.4 hours), and approximately 3.7-, 5.4-, and 52.0-fold shorter than respective therapeutic-dose half-lives. Among 5 dogs with posttreatment samples, plasma concentration rebounded after cHP in 1 naproxen-treated dog. The cHP-associated rate constant exceeded the intrinsic rate constant 11- to 40-fold in 4 of 5 dogs. Carbon hemoperfusion was associated with substantial reductions in plasma NSAID concentrations during treatment in dogs with severe ibuprofen, carprofen, or naproxen toxicosis. Most of the decline occurred early in the session. Further studies are warranted to optimize treatment protocols. Carbon hemoperfusion markedly shortened NSAID elimination half-lives in dogs with severe toxicosis, accelerating removal well beyond endogenous elimination.

papers.title: Comparison of the pharmacokinetics and sedative effects of Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan) administered intramuscularly and oral transmucosally in dogs.
papers.authors: Lathan AW, Smith CK, Kleine SA, Smith JS, Ng Z, Hampton CE, Bussieres G, Sun X, Rust MR, Knych H, Seddighi R
papers.abstract: To evaluate the sedative effects and pharmacokinetic profile of medetomidine and vatinoxan (Zenalpha) administered via the oral transmucosal (OTM) route. We hypothesized that sedation scores obtained from Zenalpha OTM (ZOTM) would not differ from Zenalpha IM (ZIM). Dogs received 20 µg/kg ZIM or 80 µg/kg ZOTM. Sedation, anxiolytic, and handling scores were collected at 0, 15, 30, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 120, 150, and 180 minutes after administration of Zenalpha. Normality was tested using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and data were presented as median and range. Physiologic data were collected at 0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 240, 360, and 480 minutes. Plasma samples were collected at 0, 3, 5, 8, 8, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 240, 360, 480, 720, and 1,440 minutes and analyzed for concentration of medetomidine and vatinoxan using LC-MS-MS. 8 healthy adult Beagles participated in this study. Dogs in ZIM and ZOTM showed significant increases in sedation, anxiolysis, and handling scores compared to baselines. Medetomidine OTM was associated with a time to maximum concentration and relative bioavailability of 86 minutes (6 minutes ZIM) and 26.4%, respectively. Vatinoxan OTM was associated with a time to maximum concentration and relative bioavailability of 216 minutes (15 minutes ZIM) and 55.2%, respectively. ZOTM (80 μg/kg) provided effective sedation, anxiolysis, and improved handling in healthy dogs comparable to ZIM (20 μg/kg) administration. Zenalpha administered OTM, at higher doses, may provide an attractive alternative to IM injection to achieve similar sedation.

papers.title: Seroprevalence of anti-Leptospira antibodies in unvaccinated hunting and guard dogs from Tiaret, northwestern Algeria: a cross-sectional study.
