papers.abstract: Canine insulinomas are functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors that typically cause hypoglycemia, but blood glucose may fluctuate before surgery and increase after resection. This report describes the diagnostic evaluation, surgical treatment, and perioperative glycemic course of a 12-year-old female Miniature Schnauzer with a pancreatic islet cell neoplasm considered clinically consistent with insulinoma. Intermittent low or low-normal blood glucose concentrations ranging from 54 to 72 mg/dL were documented before surgery, and the blood glucose concentration on the day of surgery was 73 mg/dL. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography identified a mass in the left pancreatic limb, and partial pancreatectomy was subsequently performed. Blood glucose reached 416 mg/dL 2 h after pancreatic mass removal while surgery was ongoing, then initially declined without insulin administration. Recurrent postoperative hyperglycemia was treated with regular insulin on postoperative days (PODs) 2 and 3, whereas subsequent decreases in blood glucose were treated with dextrose supplementation. Blood glucose continued to fluctuate on POD 4; no additional insulin was administered after POD 3. Histopathologic examination identified a pancreatic islet cell neoplasm. Although a paired serum insulin concentration during documented hypoglycemia was not available and immunohistochemical staining for insulin or other neuroendocrine markers was not performed, the clinical, imaging, glycemic, and histopathological findings were considered consistent with a clinicopathologic diagnosis of insulinoma. Blood glucose was 150 mg/dL on POD 7; subsequent recorded concentrations through POD 150 ranged from 107 to 133 mg/dL. Serial glucose monitoring helped characterize the perioperative course and guide postoperative insulin and dextrose treatment.

papers.title: Cytologically Suggested Vulvar Involvement in a Dog with Multicentric Lymphoma After a Nodal Response to CHOP-Based Chemotherapy, with Discordant Clonality Results: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Roh T, Song K
papers.abstract: Involvement of the female reproductive tract is rare in canine lymphoma. A 9-year-old spayed female Maltese dog was presented with generalized lymphadenopathy. Cytology of a mandibular lymph node aspirate indicated large cell lymphoma, whereas PCR for antigen receptor rearrangement (PARR) of the same sample was polyclonal. Splenectomy confirmed splenic large cell lymphoma, classified as World Health Organization clinical stage IVa. After 12 cycles of a CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone)-based protocol, restaging computed tomography showed a marked reduction in all measurable lymph nodes, whereas gastric and subcutaneous nodules persisted. On Day 181 (168 days after the start of chemotherapy), vulvar swelling was noticed and progressed despite antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatment, together with inguinal lymphadenopathy. Disease progression was diagnosed by inguinal lymph node cytology, and rescue chemotherapy was started; however, the dog developed acute dyspnea and died two days later. Results reported after death showed a mixed monoclonal and polyclonal immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgH) pattern in the inguinal lymph node and a clonal IgH rearrangement in the vulvar aspirate, which was cytologically consistent with lymphoma. In dogs treated for lymphoma, vulvar swelling may reflect neoplastic infiltration, and PARR results may differ between samples obtained at different sites and time points.

papers.title: A Salivary Conglomerate with a Substantial Organic Component Mimicking a Mineral Sialolith in the Mandibular-Sublingual Gland Complex of a Dog.
papers.authors: Schidu D, Zelinschi V, Hrițcu OM, Acomi ȘM, Ștefănescu RA, Șindilar EV, Burtan LC, Solcan G
papers.abstract: Solid lesions of the mandibular-sublingual salivary gland complex are rare in dogs. We report the case of an 11-year-old, 5 kg, intact female Maltese dog that presented with a non-painful, 2-3 cm left cervical swelling, soft at the surface and firm in depth. Fine-needle aspiration yielded clear, sero-mucous fluid. Radiographs revealed a well-defined, ovoid radiopaque structure measuring 3.1 × 2.9 cm in the cranial cervical region. Mandibular and monostomatic sublingual sialoadenectomy via a ventral approach revealed a large, heart-shaped, solid conglomerate within the glandular complex. Histopathological examination confirmed glandular atrophy, fibrosis and sialoadenitis. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometry of the submitted fragments indicated a substantial organic, protein- and lipid-rich component, with additional bands suggesting a possible minor mineral component. The dog healed completely, with no recurrence detected at the 2-week examination. Limitations include the absence of cross-sectional imaging and elemental analysis and the limited clinical follow-up. This case shows that protein-rich solid conglomerates should be included in the differential diagnosis of cervical swellings in dogs, that radiopacity alone does not establish mineral composition, and that complete surgical excision was associated with a favourable short-term outcome.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of the Fatty Acid Profiles of Hypoallergenic Veterinary Diets, Commercial Dog Foods, and Oral Fatty Acid Supplements Available on the Hungarian Market.
papers.authors: Tóth Z, Fébel H, Wágner L, Buránszki B, Lajos A, Vida K, Tarpataki N
papers.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), particularly the long-chain n-3 PUFAs (eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)), are integral to the dietary management of canine atopic dermatitis (CAD). However, the fatty acid profiles of commercially available canine products on Hungarian markets have not been systematically characterised, and the present study aimed to address this gap. A total of 35 products selected from those available on the Hungarian market at the time of sampling were analysed by gas chromatography with flame ionisation detection (GC-FID): 8 hypoallergenic veterinary diets (HVD), 22 commercial dog foods (CD), and 5 oral fatty acid supplements (FS). FS1-FS4 are complementary feeds under Regulation (EC) No 767/2009. FS5 is a food supplement under Directive 2002/46/EC. FS5 was included for comparative reference only. Fatty acid composition is expressed as % of total peak area. The n-6/n-3 ratio differed substantially across categories (HVD mean 6.16, range 2.65-10.71; CD mean 9.94, range 2.68-18.16; FS1-FS4 mean 18.08, range 0.29-63.49 (FS5 excluded as human product)). Combined % of EPA + DHA was lower in dietary products (HVD mean 0.94%, range 0.16-2.10%; CD mean 0.19%, range 0.09-0.34%) than in marine-based supplements (FS3 7.52%, FS4 24.19%). Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) was the predominant n-3 fatty acid in 29 of 30 dietary products. Pronounced inter-product heterogeneity was observed among supplements, including one plant-based product with an n-6/n-3 ratio of 63.49. These findings indicate that commercial and hypoallergenic diets contain low proportion of EPA, and that marine-based oral supplementation provided substantially higher proportions of EPA and DHA than any dietary product evaluated.

papers.title: Transosseous Suture Fixation of an Inverted Palatal Mucoperiosteal Flap to Residual Buccal Alveolar Bone for Oronasal Fistula Repair in a Dog.
papers.authors: Lee JH, Lee S, Cho JS, Park C, Park BJ, Yoon S, Jeongwon L, Kim J, Kim HY, Kim JM
papers.abstract: Advanced periodontal disease can compromise the recipient tissues available for flap fixation during oronasal fistula repair. This report describes double-layer repair of an acquired periodontal oronasal fistula in an eight-year-old castrated male Beagle. Radiographs and computed tomography (CT) identified regional bone loss and residual alveolar bone adjacent to the defect. Following extraction of the left maxillary canine and second premolar and debridement of the fistula margins, an inverted hard palatal mucoperiosteal flap was anchored to residual buccal alveolar bone through four transosseous bone holes created with an 18-gauge needle. Transosseous suture fixation used 4-0 polydioxanone simple interrupted sutures. A buccal mucosal advancement flap covered the inverted flap and palatal donor site; no interpositional graft was used. Healing without clinically evident dehiscence was documented on postoperative day 18, and nasal discharge had resolved by day 45. At 555 days, visual oral examination revealed an intact repair, with concordant CT findings obtained for an unrelated otologic indication. This case illustrates the use of residual buccal alveolar bone for palatal flap attachment when periodontal tissue loss limits gingival recipient margins, with maintained closure documented at late clinical and imaging reassessment.

papers.title: Dietary Curcumin Protects Common Carp ( Cyprinus carpio ) Against Potassium Permanganate-Induced Toxicity: Hematological, Immunological, Oxidative, and Molecular Docking Evidence.
papers.authors: Eroğlu M, Mişe Yonar S, Tanrıkulu D, Uslu H, Yonar ME
papers.abstract: Potassium permanganate treatment can adversely affect fish physiology despite its usefulness in aquaculture. This study evaluated the protective effects of dietary curcumin against potassium permanganate-induced disturbances in common carp (Cyprinus carpio). Fish were fed a basal diet or diets supplemented with 1%, 2%, or 4% curcumin for eight weeks, with or without subsequent exposure to potassium permanganate at 2 mg/L for 30 min daily for seven days. Hematological and immune parameters and oxidative status in the liver, kidney, spleen, and gill were assessed. Potassium permanganate exposure altered blood and immune parameters, increased lipid peroxidation, and weakened antioxidant defenses. Curcumin supplementation alleviated these effects, with protection evident at 1%, the lowest dietary inclusion level tested, and further improvements in selected parameters at 4%. Inclusion levels below 1% were not evaluated, so the minimum effective level remains unknown. Molecular docking predicted interactions between curcumin and the antioxidant enzymes SOD, CAT, GPx, and GST at structurally plausible binding sites. These computational findings were interpreted alongside the biological results as supportive, hypothesis-generating evidence rather than confirmation of functional effects on these enzymes in vivo. Overall, dietary curcumin showed potential to reduce the physiological disturbances associated with repeated potassium permanganate exposure. Further dose-response studies should evaluate inclusion levels below 1% to identify effective and economically viable supplementation rates and determine whether curcumin affects the antiparasitic or antibacterial efficacy of potassium permanganate.

papers.title: Clinical Diagnostic Assessment of Serum Testosterone in Intact and Castrated Tomcats.
papers.authors: Tekin K, Pereira M, Pimazzoni L, Bonsembiante F, Zucchini P, Romagnoli S
papers.abstract: Basal serum testosterone may help determine reproductive status in tomcats with an uncertain surgical history, but interpretation of a single result is limited by episodic secretion and reduced analytical precision at very low concentrations. We evaluated the analytical performance and diagnostic accuracy of an automated fluorescence enzyme immunoassay (FEIA) in 80 male cats (40 intact and 40 castrated). Within-run and between-day precision and dilutional recovery were assessed using pooled feline serum, and diagnostic performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Testosterone concentrations were significantly higher in intact than castrated cats ( p < 0.001), although overlap occurred at low concentrations. ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.773 (95% CI, 0.665-0.859). The Youden-derived threshold > 0.124 ng/mL had 60.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 43.3-75.1%) and 90.0% specificity (95% CI, 76.3-97.2%). No castrated cat had a concentration > 0.271 ng/mL; this cohort-specific rule-in threshold had 47.5% sensitivity (95% CI, 31.5-63.9%) and 100% observed specificity (95% CI, 91.2-100.0%). Therefore, clearly elevated basal testosterone can support the presence of functional testicular tissue, but concentrations ≤ 0.271 ng/mL cannot exclude intact status. Low or equivocal results require integration with clinical examination and, when indicated, GnRH stimulation and/or anti-Müllerian hormone measurement. Independent validation is required before broad clinical application.

papers.title: Hematologic Responses to Molidustat in Cats with Anemia of Heterogeneous Etiology: A Retrospective Descriptive Study.
papers.authors: Lee G, Lee J, Song KH
papers.abstract: Molidustat, an oral hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, is approved for nonregenerative anemia associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats but is also used for anemia of other causes. This retrospective, single-center study described the hematologic response to molidustat in 39 cats with anemia of heterogeneous etiology and identified factors that complicate attribution of improvement to the drug. Response was defined as a hematocrit (HCT) increase of ≥4 percentage points from baseline at the complete blood count closest to day 28 (days 14-45), without transfusion to treat anemia. Molidustat was used outside the approved indication in 33 cats (84.6%). Seventeen cats (43.6%) had a response-window measurement; they had a longer treatment span and differed in etiology and concurrent treatment from non-evaluable cats. Among these 17 cats, 12 (70.6%; 95% CI 46.9-86.7%) met the response criterion; sensitivity analyses specified before formal analysis gave 70.6-75.0% and post hoc attribution analyses 29.4-50.0%. In 7 of the 12 responders, darbepoetin or transfusion preceded the qualifying measurement, or it was obtained more than 7 days after the last dose. These data describe clinical use but do not establish effectiveness outside CKD-associated anemia.

papers.title: Detection of Zoonotic Protozoan Enteropathogens in Stray and Owned Dogs with Diarrhea in Trabzon Province Using Microscopic and Molecular Methods.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic protozoan parasites in dogs represent a significant public health concern because of their ability to infect humans. This study aimed to detect and determine the prevalence of zoonotic protozoan infections, including Balantidium coli , Entamoeba histolytica , Giardia duodenalis , Cryptosporidium spp., Sarcocystis spp. and Cystoisospora spp. in stray and owned dogs with diarrhea in Trabzon Province, Türkiye. Fecal samples were obtained from 450 dogs of various ages, sexes, and breeds. Samples were preserved in 70% alcohol for molecular analysis and incubated in 2.5% potassium dichromate for microscopic examination. Parasite DNA was analyzed using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and identified by restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP). Microscopic examination identified the Cystoisospora ohioensis group, Cystoisospora canis , and Sarcocystis spp. in 56 samples (12.44%). Specifically, Cystoisospora spp. and Sarcocystis spp. were detected in 36 (8.00%) and 20 (4.44%) of the samples, respectively. A mixed infection involving C. canis and the C. ohioensis group was observed in one sample. Molecular analyses detected Cystoisospora spp. DNA in 36 samples (8.00%) and Sarcocystis spp. DNA in 20 samples (4.44%). RFLP analysis confirmed that all detected Cystoisospora spp. DNA belonged to C. ohioensis , while Sarcocystis spp. could not be differentiated at the species level. This study reports the first microscopic detection of Sarcocystis spp. and C. ohioensis in dogs in Trabzon Province and constitutes the first molecular identification of C. ohioensis in Türkiye.

papers.title: Correction to "A Rare Case of Cutaneous Infection by Corynascus verrucosus in a Shih Tzu Dog: Molecular Identification and Phylogenetic Analysis".
Hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension under isoflurane anesthesia.
papers.authors: Seki D, Kusu H, Fujimoto T, Kitagawa H, Goya S, Yamaya Y, Teshima K
papers.abstract: While dopamine and dobutamine are widely used in anesthetized dogs, clinical evidence supporting their use remains limited. We aimed to compare the hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension undergoing elective orthopedic surgery under fentanyl-isoflurane anesthesia. The pressor effects at clinical dosages (2-8 µg/kg/min) of dopamine (n = 15) and dobutamine (n = 15) for hypotension were compared and confirmed using the ramped-rate infusion protocol in 30 dogs. The following hemodynamic parameters measured by invasive arterial blood pressure and transesophageal echocardiographic monitoring were analyzed: heart rate (HR), systolic (SAP), mean (MAP), diastolic arterial pressure (DAP), stroke volume index (SVI), cardiac index (CI), and systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI). The proportion of dogs that achieved the treatment goal (MAP: 70-89 mmHg) was 93% (dopamine responders, 14/15 dogs) in the dopamine group and 53% (dobutamine responders, 8/15 dogs) in the dobutamine group, with a significantly higher probability in the dopamine group (P = 0.035, a risk difference of 40% [95% confidence interval: 8.2-63.9%]). In dopamine responders, significant increases were observed in SAP, MAP, DAP, SVI and CI, whereas no significant changes were observed in HR and SVRI. In conclusion, the pressor effect was more likely to be observed at the clinical dosage of dopamine than that of dobutamine for treating hypotension in isoflurane anesthetized dogs. This study was approved by the Nihon University Animal Medical Center Research and Trial Ethics Committee (approval number: 1-007; approval date: September 29, 2022).

papers.title: Histomorphometric characterization of cardiac nodes in cattle, ponies, and cats.
papers.authors: Gómez-Torres F, Ballesteros-Acuña L, Ruíz-Saurí A
papers.abstract: The sinoatrial node (SAN) and atrioventricular node (AVN) are essential components of the cardiac conduction system and play a critical role in initiating and propagating the electrical impulse. To characterize these cardiac nodes across different species, we examined the hearts of ten cattle, ten cats, and five male ponies without evidence of cardiac disease using conventional histological and immunohistochemical techniques. Morphometric parameters of the nodes and their constituent cells were quantified at different magnifications. The SAN displayed an oval morphology in all species. Its diameter was 888.58 ± 6.36 μm in cats, 2143.17 ± 199.13 μm in ponies, and 2033.28 ± 939.44 μm in cattle. Mean nodal density was significantly higher in ponies than in cattle (p = 0.011). Pacemaker (P) cells of the AVN were significantly larger in ungulate species than in cats (p < 0.001). Heart bone (os cordis) was identified in all ten cattle hearts and in one cat heart, showing typical features of compact bone and bone marrow. Cartilaginous metaplasia was observed in all pony hearts and in 60% of cat hearts and was associated with reduced AVN size and cellularity in cats. These findings highlight important interspecies differences and contribute to the understanding of conduction system pathology in veterinary cardiology. The structural changes in the cardiac nodes in these species warrant more in-depth functional research, given the lack of functional cardiac assessment and the small sample size.

papers.title: Echocardiographic description of pulmonary vein stenosis in a cat with atrioventricular septal defect.
papers.authors: Seyednejad F, Locquet L, Ardehali P, Astaraki N
papers.abstract: A 2.5-year-old, intact female British Shorthair cat was referred for cardiology evaluation owing to intermittent panting and a heart murmur identified on cardiac auscultation before elective surgery. Physical examination revealed a left parasternal grade II/VI systolic murmur without arrhythmia. Thoracic radiographs showed cardiomegaly without pulmonary infiltration. The echocardiography was prompted by auscultation, history and radiological findings. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated marked right atrial enlargement and eccentric hypertrophy of the right ventricle. Echocardiography revealed a partial atrioventricular septal defect characterised by a large ostium primum defect (0.79 cm) and an anterior mitral valve cleft, resulting in a left-to-right shunt (estimated Qp:Qs ≈ 2.2). Doppler interrogation of the left pulmonary vein entering the lateral wall of the left atrium demonstrated focal turbulence and increased peak velocity (1.08 m/s), corresponding to a pressure gradient of approximately 4.7 mmHg, findings consistent with suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. Tricuspid regurgitation velocity (2.2 m/s) did not reflect increased afterload. Elective surgery was postponed owing to uncertainty regarding peri-anaesthetic haemodynamic risk. Medical treatment with enalapril and clopidogrel was initiated. At the 9-month follow-up, the cat remained clinically stable and echocardiographic findings were unchanged. Pulmonary vein stenosis is rarely reported in cats. This report describes the concurrent presence of partial atrioventricular septal defect and suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. These findings highlight the detection of a congenital heart defect in a young cat, despite the low-grade murmur. A rare congenital heart condition in a British Shorthair cat A 2.5-year-old, female British Shorthair cat was referred for a heart check after intermittent panting and a heart murmur were noticed before planned elective surgery. Examination confirmed a mild heart murmur and chest radiography showed an enlarged heart. Heart ultrasound revealed a congenital heart defect called a partial atrioventricular septal defect. This means there was an abnormal opening between the upper chambers of the heart, together with an abnormality of the mitral valve. These changes caused increased blood flow from the left side of the heart to the right side, leading to enlargement of the right side of the heart. The ultrasound also showed abnormal blood flow in one of the pulmonary veins, raising suspicion of narrowing of that vein. Because of the heart findings and possible anaesthetic risk, the planned surgery was postponed. The cat was started on medical treatment and remained stable after 9 months, with no worsening of the heart ultrasound findings. This case is important because pulmonary vein stenosis is rarely reported in cats, especially alongside this type of congenital heart disease. It also shows that even a mild heart murmur in a young cat can be associated with significant underlying heart abnormalities.

papers.title: Proactive Treatment of Canine Allergic Otitis Externa With Hydrocortisone Aceponate: A Retrospective Observational Study.
papers.authors: Maina E, Rigert JC, Filippini C, Cao R, Oliveira A
papers.abstract: Allergic otitis externa is common in dogs and recurrence may lead to repeated consultations and antimicrobial use. Long-term data on proactive topical corticosteroid maintenance are limited. To describe 12-month relapse frequency in dogs with allergic otitis externa receiving proactive hydrocortisone aceponate maintenance therapy and compare consecutive-day and non-consecutive-day schedules. Medical records of client-owned dogs prescribed hydrocortisone aceponate ear spray were retrospectively reviewed. Maintenance started after clinical and cytological remission. Only dogs with confirmed continuation, stable concomitant allergy management and complete 12-month outcome data were included. Relapse was defined as recurrent otitis externa requiring veterinary examination, cytology and additional otic treatment. Dogs were grouped by schedule: Protocol 1, two consecutive days; and Protocol 2, two non-consecutive days weekly. Outcomes were compared using Fisher exact and Mann-Whitney U tests. Seventy-one dogs were included; 36 in Protocol 1 and 35 received Protocol 2. During 12 months, 50/71 dogs (70.4%) had no relapse, 12/71 (16.9%) had one relapse and 9/71 (12.7%) had multiple relapses. At least one relapse occurred in 9/36 dogs (25.0%) in Protocol 1 and 12/35 (34.3%) receiving Protocol 2 (p = 0.443). Multiple relapses occurred in 2/36 (5.6%) and 7/35 (20.0%) dogs, respectively (p = 0.085). Relapse counts did not differ significantly between protocols (p = 0.290). Most dogs had no relapse or only one relapse during proactive hydrocortisone aceponate maintenance. No statistically significant difference was detected between schedules, but equivalence or non-inferiority cannot be concluded.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Experimental Evaluation of the Immunogenicity of Feline Erythrocyte Antigen 6 (FEA 6) in Transfusion-Naive FEA 6-Negative Cats.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Bangash MY, Blais MC
papers.abstract: ObjectivesFeline Erythrocyte Antigen 6 (FEA 6) is a newly identified red blood cell (RBC) antigen in cats discovered following an unintentional sensitization event, suggesting it can be immunogenic. Its ability to consistently induce alloimmunization remains unknown. This prospective study evaluated FEA 6 immunogenicity in transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative cats by assessing anti-FEA 6 alloantibody production and plasma levels. A secondary objective was to bank polyclonal anti-FEA 6 antibodies.MethodsFifty-three cats underwent AB and extensive blood typing for FEAs 1-6, naturally occurring alloantibody (NOAb) screening, and compatibility testing to select donor-recipient pairs. FEA 6 prevalence was assessed in 82 type A cats. Two transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative cats received FEA 6-positive, otherwise compatible RBC transfusions and were monitored for anti-FEA 6 alloantibody production by gel column agglutination. Repeat transfusions were performed if alloantibodies became undetectable. Agreement between recipient-derived and reference anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies was evaluated in 51 type A cats using kappa statistics.ResultsFEA 6 prevalence among type A cats was 75.6% (62/82); NOAb were detected in 10.3% of screened type A cats, but none were directed against FEA 6. Both recipients developed anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies. Recipient 1 responded after two sensitizations, whereas recipient 2 responded after a single transfusion. Both reached peak titers of 1:8, with alloantibodies detectable through days 372 and 200, respectively. Recipient-derived anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies showed substantial agreement with the reference anti-FEA 6 antibody (κ = 0.64-0.78, P < .001) and almost perfect agreement with each other (κ = 0.87, P < .001).Conclusions and relevanceTransfusion of FEA 6-positive RBCs induced anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies in all transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative recipients, supporting FEA 6 immunogenicity and its likely contribution to unexplained post-transfusion alloantibodies in cats. The resulting polyclonal antibodies may support FEA 6 typing and transfusion research, although more durable reagents remain needed.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Mineral Analysis of Feline Treats: Unrecognized Sources of Phosphorus and Calcium in the Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Harris AN, Harris T, Vaden S
papers.abstract: Dietary phosphorus restriction is a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease (CKD) management in cats. While therapeutic renal diets are formulated to limit phosphorus intake, treats also contribute to total dietary phosphorus and calcium intake. The objective of this study was to quantify the phosphorus and calcium content of some feline purée-style treats and evaluate their potential contribution to dietary mineral intake in cats with CKD. A convenience sample comprising four flavors of commercially available Inaba Churu purée treats and three flavors of Weurva low-phosphorus purée treats were analyzed. Phosphorus and calcium concentrations were quantified using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry and reported descriptively as milligrams per sachet and milligrams per 100 kcal. Phosphorus content varied widely across products, ranging from 9 to 36 mg per sachet (64-600mg/100kcal). The evaluated Churu treats contained higher phosphorus concentrations (29-36 mg/ sachet) than the evaluated Weruva low-phosphorus formulations (9-10 mg/sachet). Calcium concentrations ranged from 0.14 to 4.06 mg per sachet (2.3-67.7 mg/100 kcal), with corresponding calcium-to-phosphorus (Ca:P) ratios ranging from 0.004 to 0.119. Phosphorus and calcium content, including Ca:P ratios, varied substantially among the products evaluated. These differences should be considered as part of the overall dietary management of cats with CKD, particularly when treats are administered routinely.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Assessment of an educational social media campaign on improving feline osteoarthritis pain awareness and knowledge among cat owners.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Wong WS, Alcântara H, Bukhari SSUH, Murrell J, Steagall P
papers.abstract: Objectives - Feline osteoarthritis (OA) is highly prevalent but often underdiagnosed, largely owing to owners' difficulty recognising subtle clinical signs. This study evaluated the effects of an evidence-based, peer-reviewed educational social media campaign on cat owners' knowledge and awareness of feline OA.Methods - A prospective, interventional study was conducted with a convenience sample of adult, non-veterinary cat owners recruited via social media. Participants completed a validated online survey assessing knowledge and attitudes about feline OA before and after viewing an evidence based social media campaign (i.e., the intervention) covering 4 domains (introduction, clinical signs, diagnosis, management). Paired non parametric tests compared pre- and post-intervention total knowledge scores, individual knowledge items and Likert scale attitude items.Results - A total of 53 participants completed both surveys. Mean total knowledge scores increased from 19.9 ± 3.1 to 23.6 ± 2.8 (p < 0.001). Correct identification of OA as non-curable increased from 49.1% to 83% (p < 0.001), and the misconception that OA only affects senior cats decreased from 13.2% to 0% (p = 0.02). Recognition of key risk factors improved: neutering after 6 months of age (9.4% to 60.4%, p < 0.001) and outdoor access (28.3% to 73.6%, p < 0.001). Recognition of scratching posts as an option for environment changes increased from 24.5% to 60.3% (p <0.001). The owners' confidence in their ability to contribute to diagnosis increased (Hodges-Lehmann shift +0.99, p = 0.04), knowledge of environmental modifications increased (+1.49, p <0.001), and stress about lifelong management decreased (-0.99, p = 0.01). Most participants (≥91%) found the intervention materials enjoyable and useful; 96% would share the content with others.Conclusion and relevance - An evidence-based educational social media campaign significantly improved cat owners' awareness and knowledge regarding feline OA, suggesting a scalable platform to complement traditional veterinarian-client communication.

papers.title: Use of plasma chromogranin a epitopes vasostatin and catestatin as biomarkers for catecholamine-producing tumours in dogs.
papers.authors: Prabert J, Hanson J, Ishigaki K, Asano K, Höglund K, Stridsberg M, Höglund OV
papers.abstract: Differentiation of catecholamine-producing tumours from other adrenal tumours remains difficult. Chromogranin A (CgA) is a marker for catecholamine secretion in the body. An assay for quantification of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin has been validated for use in dogs but not yet evaluated in dogs with catecholamine-producing tumours. The aims were to evaluate the assays foranalysis of plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin in dogs with adrenal tumours and to compare concentrations between catecholamine-producing tumours and adrenocortical tumours in dogs that were subjected to adrenalectomy. Twelve dogs with histopathologically confirmed catecholamine-secreting tumours (eleven pheochromocytomas (PCCs), one extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma (PGL)) and twelve with adrenocortical tumours were included in the study. Plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin were determined byradioimmunoassay (RIA), before adrenalectomy in 23 out of 24 dogs and after adrenalectomy in six of the dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours (five PCC, one PGL). Tumour diagnosis was made by histopathology in all cases. Overall, median plasma concentration of the CgA epitopevasostatin in dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours was 0.82 nmol/L (interquartile range (IQR) 0.52 to 1.60 nmol/L), which was significantly higher(Wilcoxon rank sum exact test, P= 0.0374) than the vasostatin concentration in adrenocortical tumours (median 0.50; IQR 0.34 to 0.59 nmol/L). A subsetof dogs (5/12) with catecholamine-secreting tumours had elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations preoperatively. After successful surgery, thepreoperatively elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations decreased numerically, however without reaching statistical significance. Catestatin concentrationdid not differ between tumour types. Elevated plasma concentration of the CgA epitope vasostatin showed potential as a biomarker for asubset of catecholamine-secreting tumours.

papers.title: Spontaneous tumors in dogs and cats in Algeria: a dual-source descriptive study of practitioner-reported patterns and histopathology-submitted cases.
papers.authors: Bouchoukh AS, Boukhechem S, Bougherara H, Chaabi AZ
papers.abstract: Algeria has no documented national companion-animal cancer registry, and limited information is available on tumors encountered in veterinary practice or reaching histopathological confirmation. This dual-source descriptive study combined two independently analyzed components: a histopathology-based descriptive case series of diagnostic tumor submissions from dogs and cats, and a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of veterinarians practicing in Algeria. The first component characterized tumors reaching histopathological confirmation, whereas the second examined practitioner-reported tumor patterns, perceived diagnostic-resource availability, and self-reported preparedness. The histopathology-based case series comprised 86 tumor submissions from 81 animals accrued between March 2022 and March 2025. Mammary tumors were the largest category (43/86; 50.0%), followed by cutaneous/subcutaneous tumors (20/86; 23.3%); 80 tumors (93.0%) were classified as malignant. Among 162 questionnaire responses collected between October 2024 and May 2025, 111 respondents selected "dogs and cats" as their main animal group. Mammary tumors were reported by 109 respondents (98.2%), cutaneous/subcutaneous tumors by 79 (71.2%), and canine transmissible venereal tumor (CTVT) by 54 (48.6%); multiple categories could be reported. The most frequent self-reported preparedness rating was "Moderately prepared" (52/111; 46.8%), while 99 of 110 respondents with valid data (90.0%) rated diagnostic resources as either "Insufficient" or "Not at all satisfactory." Mammary and cutaneous/subcutaneous tumors ranked first and second in both sources, whereas the rankings of the remaining categories differed. Because the sources represented different populations, analytical units, denominators, and diagnostic pathways, the comparison was restricted to an exploratory descriptive assessment and was not interpreted as evidence of differences in population-level tumor occurrence. This study provides an initial structured account of companion-animal tumor documentation in Algeria. The partial agreement between the two sources, together with unfavorable diagnostic-availability ratings, suggests potential gaps between clinical recognition, histopathological confirmation, and systematic recording. Standardized submission and coding procedures, improved specimen-transport and formal pathology-referral pathways, broader geographic participation, and progressive development of companion-animal cancer registration are needed to strengthen the national evidence base.

papers.title: Biological response stability of refrigerated cosacthen after opening and non-hormonal effects of ACTH stimulation testing in healthy dogs.
papers.authors: de Oliveira MC, Nogueira TB, Gouvêa FL, Oliveira JM, Trevizan L, Pöppl ÁG
papers.abstract: The adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test (ACTHST) is widely used to evaluate adrenal reserve in dogs. This study assessed the effects of refrigerated storage of tetracosactide (Cosacthen) after opening for up to three weeks and investigated hematological, biochemical, and electrolyte changes following ACTH stimulation. Ten healthy beagle dogs (five males and five females) were enrolled. Each dog received tetracosactide (5 μg/kg, IV) at vial opening (T0) and at 7-day intervals over 3 weeks (T1 to T3), using aliquots from the same vial stored at 2-8°C. Blood samples were collected before and 1 hour after ACTH administration to measure cortisol, hematology, biochemistry, and electrolytes. Clinical monitoring was performed after each test. Cortisol concentrations increased significantly after ACTH administration at all time points (T0-T3). Delta-cortisol was higher at T1 than at T0 (P = 0.0104) and lower at T2 than at T1 (P = 0.0059), with no differences among T0, T2, and T3. After ACTH administration, red blood cell count, hematocrit, hemoglobin, albumin, alkaline phosphatase, triglycerides, cholesterol, potassium, and total calcium decreased significantly, whereas glucose increased. All values remained within reference intervals, and no adverse effects were observed. Refrigerated storage of Cosacthen after opening did not alter cortisol responses. Post-ACTH changes in laboratory variables should be considered when interpreting results.

papers.title: Ultrasonographic Features of Pleural Thickening in Cats With Pulmonary Carcinoma and Pleural Effusion: A Retrospective Descriptive Study.
papers.authors: Toshima A, Fulkerson CV, Murakami M
papers.abstract: Pleural involvement is an important but poorly described manifestation of feline pulmonary carcinoma. Thoracic ultrasonography may identify pleural abnormalities and accessible targets for cytologic sampling in cats with pleural effusion. To describe ultrasonographic features of pleural thickening in cats with pulmonary carcinoma and pleural effusion and summarise cytologic findings from pleural effusion and ultrasound-guided lesion sampling. Medical records from one referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed for cats with pulmonary carcinoma or metastatic epithelial neoplasia consistent with pulmonary origin, pleural effusion, and stored thoracic ultrasound images. Images were reviewed in consensus by three observers for distribution, location, shape, maximal thickness, echogenicity, homogeneity, and suspected intercostal muscle invasion. Twenty-two cats were included. Pleural thickening was recorded in all cats. Thickening was classified as diffuse in 12 cats, focal in 6, and multifocal in 4; however, scanning was not systematic across all thoracic regions. The representative or measured pleural abnormality was in the cranial pleural region in 18 cats. Maximal pleural thickness was 5.6 ± 3.3 mm (median, 4.9 mm; range, 1.2-16.2 mm). Suspected intercostal muscle invasion was recorded in eight cats. Neoplastic cells were identified in pleural effusion cytology in 15/20 cats. Six cats underwent ultrasound-guided lesion sampling; cytologic or histopathologic findings were supportive of carcinoma in all 6, including 1 confirmed by biopsy. In this selected cohort, thoracic ultrasonography identified pleural thickening with variable morphology. Thickened pleura may represent a feasible sampling target, but prospective studies are needed to determine prevalence, distribution, sensitivity, and specificity.

papers.title: Morpho-molecular assessment of nanomaterials in teleost fish wound healing: a systematic review.
papers.authors: Rabea A, Ibrahim I, Mahgoub H, El-Shaieb A
papers.abstract: Teleost fish skin is a vital barrier for regulating osmoregulation, immune defense, and respiration. Cutaneous wounds in farmed fish cause significant economic loss and welfare concerns, as standard treatments, like antibiotics and chemical baths, are often ineffective, toxic, and fail to adhere to mucus-covered surfaces. While nanomaterials show great promise for wound healing, current data on how they work in fish remain incomplete. This systematic review evaluates the performance of these nanomaterials, explains their healing mechanisms, and highlights the key research gaps to guide future aquaculture treatments. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we included twelve in vivo studies (2017-2026). A clear shift was observed over time: research before 2020 focused only on metallic nanoparticles (silver and zinc oxide), whereas recent studies have mostly used biopolymeric nano-delivery systems. Nanoparticle treatments consistently led to faster wound closure, with several formulas healing over 90% of the wound within two weeks; however, these quantitative outcomes are strictly descriptive due to high methodological heterogeneity across studies. Under the microscope, nanomaterials accelerated re-epithelialization, improved collagen organization, and reduced inflammation. At the molecular level, they decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, TNFα) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPS), while increasing anti-inflammatory markers (IL10, TGF-β) and antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT). Transcriptomics data also showed the activation of fibroblast growth factor 7 (FGF7) and the Jak-STAT pathways. Finally, zebrafish (Danio rerio) constituted 75% of the study models, showing a major gap in research on farmed fish like Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). This systematic review shows that nanomaterials significantly accelerate teleost wound healing by promoting tissue regeneration and regulating the immune response. The shift toward biopolymeric systems, especially chitosan, indicates a clear trend toward safe and sustainable aquaculture medicine. Notably, testing hybrid nano-hyaluronic acid and nano-chitosan systems remains completely unexplored in farmed fish. This gap is important due to the complementary biological properties of these materials and the high global value of Nile tilapia. Testing this hybrid biomaterial under real farming conditions will help improve skin healing, support the immune system, and provide a safe wound treatment for global aquaculture.

papers.title: Developmental lung disease with associated pulmonary hypertension in a Sphynx kitten.
papers.authors: Martin E, Wiggen KE, Williams K, Masseau I, Reinero CR
papers.abstract: This case report describes the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings and clinicopathologic features consistent with developmental lung disease (DLD) and pulmonary hypertension (PH) in a 3-month-old Sphynx Munchkin kitten. The kitten was originally referred for episodes of respiratory distress that was unresponsive to medical management, consisting of diuretics, antibiotics and corticosteroids. Echocardiography was consistent with a high probability of PH of a non-cardiac etiology. Baseline blood work, thoracic radiographs, thoracic CT with triphasic angiography and a bronchoalveolar lavage were performed. Thoracic CT revealed diffuse ground-glass opacity with bronchiolectasis and distention of the pulmonary artery and branches. The bronchoalveolar lavage identified an equal distribution of non-degenerative neutrophils and macrophages, with erythrophagocytosis and no overt neoplastic cells or infectious organisms identified. The kitten was humanely euthanized due to the lack of an identifiable treatable etiology and poor prognosis. Histopathological findings were most consistent with DLD with diffuse acinar underdevelopment and vascular changes including pulmonary capillary hemangiomatosis. These findings have not been previously reported in the feline DLD literature. There is a paucity of literature describing DLD and its potential to cause PH in cats. A comprehensive diagnostic evaluation, ultimately including histologic examination, is needed to reach a diagnosis of DLD. The presence of PH in a young kitten without any identifiable primary cardiac or respiratory cause, pulmonary thromboembolism or cardiac parasites should lead to a DLD being considered.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Metagenomic Oxford Nanopore sequencing of feline aural inflammatory polyps for pathogen discovery.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Noland E, Conner K, Brame B, Petersen A, Thaiwong-Nebelung T
papers.abstract: ObjectivesFeline aural inflammatory polyps (FIAP) have been proposed to be induced by chronic viral or bacterial infections; however, the cause is still unknown. The aim of this study was to investigate potential etiologies of these polyps using metagenomic sequencing.MethodsPolyp tissue was collected from 13 cats following routine traction and avulsion procedures. Total nucleic acid was extracted and subjected to a host (feline) nucleic acid depletion protocol. Additionally, the Sequence-Independent Single-Primer Amplification (SISPA) method was used to enrich for low-abundance RNA viral genomes. Sequencing was conducted on the Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing platform. Non-feline sequencing reads were taxonomically classified against custom bacterial/viral databases to calculate relative genus-level abundances.ResultsTaxonomic classification of sequencing reads identified various bacteria across samples and, in some samples, rare viruses. However, no common microbial sequences were associated with polyps to suggest a specific infectious etiology. Bacterial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Bacillota phyla, with Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota being more frequently dominant. Lasallevirus was detected in few samples with unknown clinical relevance. Culture and sequencing showed partial concordance in identifying bacteria in some cases.Conclusions and relevanceNo common microbial-associated sequences found to be associated with polyp samples; therefore, no suspect causative agent was identified. 16S and ITS metagenomic sequencing on FIAP may help further elucidate if microbial population shifts have a role in polyp development and recurrence and/or persistence of inflammation leading to polyp development.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Assessment of caregiver burden in feline chronic kidney disease.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Lim L, Quimby JM, Caney S
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate caregiver burden associated with management of cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD).MethodsCaregivers who had experience managing a cat with CKD were recruited through social media to anonymously participate in an online Qualtrics survey. The modified Zarit Burden Interview (mZBI) was incorporated into the survey to objectively assess caregiver burden. An mZBI score of ≥ 18 represents clinically significant burden.ResultsA total of 339 surveys were completed. 46% of caregivers reported an mZBI score of ≥ 18. Caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 3/4 had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0, range 3 - 50) than caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 1/2 (median 14.5, range 0 - 58; P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported never to rarely sharing care responsibilities had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0; range 0 - 50) than those who reported sometimes to always sharing care responsibilities (median 15.0; range 2 - 58) (P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported the need to coax their cat to eat on a daily basis had higher mZBI scores (median 22.8, range 2 - 50) than those who never coaxed their cat to eat (median 14.5, range 0-49) or coaxed their cat 1-2 days/week (median 19.2, range 3 - 42) (both P < 0.001). Caregivers who always felt supported by the veterinary care team had lower mZBI scores (median 13; range 0-58) than those that only felt supported sometimes to never (median 23; range 5-45) (P < 0.001).Conclusions and clinical importanceSignificant caregiver burden is present in feline CKD, emphasizing the need to for clinicians to provide empathetic advice and practical support.

papers.title: Reassessing neonatal hypoglycemia in kittens: Clinical relevance beyond the laboratory value.
papers.authors: de Oliveira NMS, Carneiro MD, Talieri IC, Milken VMF, Gouvêa FN, Borin-Crivellenti S, Crivellenti LZ
papers.abstract: The underdeveloped metabolism in newborn kittens, along with the quick use of liver sugar reserves and the limited ability to produce glucose, makes them prone to low blood sugar levels during this time. This condition may be potentially fatal, although reduced blood glucose values do not necessarily manifest with clinical signs. Fifteen neonatal kittens born to three clinically healthy pregnant queens were evaluated during the first three days of life. Apgar scoring was done daily, and blood glucose measurements began within the first hour after birth (T1), followed by evaluations every 2 hours, with a total of six measurements each day from T2 to T6. Samples were obtained via capillary puncture with alternating digital pads and analyzed using a glucometer validated for cats. A total of 270 glycemic measurements were performed, demonstrating instability during the first hours of life. On the first day, there was a mean glucose concentration of 61.7 ± 22.2 mg/dL. On the second day, it dropped to 53.9 ± 16.5 mg/dL. On the third day, metabolic recovery occurred (68.5 ± 14.7 mg/dL). All neonates maintained adequate Apgar scores and showed no clinical signs of hypoglycemia (< 50 mg/dL; weakness, apathy, or reduced suckling reflex). Marked fluctuations in blood glucose levels were observed during the first 48 hours, characterized by wide glycemic variability (22-165 mg/dL on day 1 and 21-86 mg/dL on day 2). A high frequency of hypoglycemic values was recorded, reaching 51.1% on the first day and 60% on the second, indicating initial metabolic instability despite intermediate mean glucose levels. Progressive stabilization was observed by the third day (range 26-95 mg/dL), with the rate of hypoglycemic events dropping to 22.2%, reflecting the maturation of neonatal metabolic homeostasis. Despite the laboratory diagnosis of hypoglycemia, none of the kittens exhibited clinical manifestations or required intervention.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Evaluation of Left Atrial Reservoir Strain by Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography in Cats with Stage B1 Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Algan D, Varlik T, Bach MBT, Gleerup CH, Yilmaz Z, Koch J
papers.abstract: Left atrial reservoir strain (LA S_R), assessed by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE), reflects left atrial (LA) function and may reveal subtle alterations in LA mechanics in cats with American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM) stage B1 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) compared with healthy cats. This study aimed to determine whether LA S_R differs between cats with HCM (stage B1) and healthy cats using 2D-STE. Sixty-one client-owned cats were retrospectively identified and included from medical databases. These cats were classified as healthy controls (Stage A; n=30) or preclinical HCM (Stage B1; n=31) according to ACVIM consensus guidelines. All cats underwent a comprehensive conventional echocardiographic examination, including two-dimensional, M-mode, color Doppler, pulsed-wave Doppler, and tissue Doppler imaging, as part of clinical care or screening protocols. Conventional two-dimensional assessment of LA size and function included the LA/Ao ratio, LA diameter, LA area, LA fractional shortening (LA FS), and LA ejection fraction (LA EF). LA S_R was subsequently measured offline using automated function imaging software. Reproducibility was assessed via intra- and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to compare the discriminatory performance of LA S_R and the evaluated LA variables between the predefined study groups. Cats with ACVIM stage B1 HCM had significantly lower LA S_R than healthy controls (19.0% [IQR, 14.5-22.0%] vs 38.0% [IQR, 30.25-42.50%], respectively; P < 0.001). LA S_R reproducibility was high with an intra-observer ICC of 0.974 and an inter-observer ICC of 0.894. Assessment of LA S_R was feasible in cats with stage B1 HCM. LA S_R values differed between affected cats and healthy controls, with lower values observed in the affected group and good reproducibility. These findings suggest that LA S_R may provide complementary information on LA function in cats with this stage of disease.

papers.title: Successful management of nesidioblastosis in a dog with persistent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia following staged bilateral partial pancreatectomies.
papers.authors: Teyssandier S, Rendon ME, Lameroli H, Centurion B, Galac S
papers.abstract: Nesidioblastosis is a rare but important differential diagnosis for hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia in dogs, a condition most commonly associated with insulinoma. A nine-year-old spayed female dog was presented with recurrent episodes of collapse and documented hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Diagnostic imaging failed to identify a pancreatic mass, prompting exploratory laparotomy with left partial pancreatectomy and regional lymphadenectomy. Histopathological examination excluded insulinoma and established a diagnosis of nesidioblastosis. Although clinical signs initially resolved following surgery, hypoglycemia recurred 45 days later, prompting a right partial pancreatectomy. Following the second procedure, the patient remained euglycemic and free of clinical signs, without evidence of clinical diabetes mellitus or exocrine pancreatic insufficiency throughout an eight-month follow-up period. This case underscores the importance of considering nesidioblastosis in dogs with hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia when a pancreatic mass is not identified. Furthermore, this case suggests that recurrence after unilateral partial pancreatectomy may occur because of the diffuse nature of nesidioblastosis. In this patient, staged bilateral partial pancreatectomy was associated with sustained glycemic control and clinical remission, without clinically apparent endocrine or exocrine pancreatic dysfunction during an eight-month follow-up period.

papers.title: De Ritis ratio and L-FABP as supportive biomarkers of hepatic involvement in cats with effusive FIP.
papers.authors: Gulersoy E, Erturk A, Kısmet E
papers.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP), caused by feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), is a systemic disease affecting multiple organs. Although routine biochemical parameters are not diagnostic, they may aid in clinical suspicion. The aim of this study was to investigate the clinical utility of the De Ritis ratio (AST/ALT) and liver-type fatty acid-binding protein (L-FABP) as candidate biomarkers of liver-associated biochemical alterations in cats with effusive FIP. A total of 47 client-owned cats naturally infected with feline coronavirus (FCoV) were included: 37 cats with suspected effusive FIP (thoracic effusion, n = 14; abdominal effusion, n = 23) and 10 FCoV-positive asymptomatic cats as controls. FIPV infection was confirmed by RT-PCR of thoracic or abdominal effusion samples in all cats with suspected effusive FIP. Control cats were clinically healthy, FCoV-positive by fecal RT-PCR, and had no evidence of FIPV infection. The De Ritis ratio was significantly higher in cats with abdominal effusive FIP than in asymptomatic FCoV-positive controls and demonstrated excellent discriminatory performance for identifying abdominal effusive FIP (AUC = 0.843) and effusive FIP overall (AUC = 0.808). Although serum L-FABP concentrations did not differ significantly between groups, ROC analysis demonstrated acceptable-to-excellent discriminatory performance for cats with effusive FIP (AUC = 0.730-0.854), suggesting complementary rather than standalone clinical utility. These findings suggest that the De Ritis ratio may represent a supportive indicator of liver-associated biochemical alterations in cats with effusive FIP, whereas the clinical utility of L-FABP remains preliminary and warrants further clinical validation.

papers.title: Evaluation of urinary biomarkers for detection of renal tubular injury in Vipera berus-envenomated and critically ill dogs with and without clinically apparent acute kidney injury.
papers.authors: Selin AK, Lilliehöök I, Strage EM, Larsson A, Pelander L
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs has high mortality and early diagnosis is essential, but traditional markers are not sensitive enough to detect renal injury in the absence of decreased glomerular filtration rate. The objective of this study was to compare urinary cystatin C (uCysC), N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase (uNAG), and glucose (uGlu) among dogs hospitalised because of envenomation by Vipera berus (EVB) or admitted for intensive care without (IC) or with (AKI APP ) clinically apparent AKI, and 30 healthy dogs. Urine and serum samples were collected on days 1 and 2, and urine samples on days 7 and 14. Urinary CysC, NAG, and glucose concentrations were measured with an automated chemistry analyser, normalised to urinary creatinine concentration (uCr) and compared among groups. Ninety-seven dogs were included (30 HC, 28 EVB, 14 AKI APP and 25 IC dogs). Age, bodyweight, and sex did not differ among groups. On day 1, median [IQR] uCysC/uCr (10 -3 ) and uGlu/uCr were higher (p < 0.008) in EVB (0.05 [0.03-0.11], 0.04 [0.03-0.06)]), IC (0.06 [0.03-0.4], 0.05 [0.03-0.09]), and AKI APP (4.4 [0.13-30.0], 0.12 [0.05-0.45]) groups, compared to healthy dogs (0.02 [0.01-0.03], 0.03 [0.02-0.04]). Urinary markers decreased over two weeks post hospitalisation in all groups except AKI APP . Initial levels of uCysC/uCr were higher (p < 0.002) and remained elevated in non-survivors compared to survivors of AKI APP , suggesting potential prognostic value. Urinary CysC/uCr and Glu/uCr are potential markers of tubular injury in early stages of AKI in dogs.

papers.title: Correction: Clinico-pathological and renal morphological findings in dogs naturally infected with Dirofilaria repens.
papers.authors: Szabó KÉ, Aresu L, Müller L, Szilágyi E, Falus FA, Balogh N, Boros M, Papp T, Manczur F

papers.title: Baicalin alleviates Trueperella pyogenes-induced endometritis with associated changes in gut microbiota composition.
papers.authors: Peng Z, Gou C, Guan Y, Wang Y, Liu Y, Wang F, Wang R, Qi M
papers.abstract: Endometritis is a prevalent reproductive disorder in livestock characterized by inflammation, oxidative stress, and microbial imbalance; however, the mechanistic links among these processes remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the protective effects of baicalin in a Trueperella pyogenes (T. pyogenes)-induced mouse model of endometritis by integrating network pharmacology, in vivo validation, and gut microbiota profiling. Network pharmacology analysis identified prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2, also known as cyclooxygenase-2, COX-2) and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) as key targets of baicalin, with enrichment in arachidonic acid metabolism pathways. Baicalin treatment alleviated uterine pathology and suppressed inflammatory responses, as indicated by reduced tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity. Baicalin also restored redox homeostasis by activating the Nrf2/Keap1/HO-1 pathway, increasing catalase (CAT) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activities while decreasing malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and concurrently reduced apoptosis, as evidenced by a lower ratio of Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax) to B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2) (the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio). Concurrently, 16 S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that baicalin treatment was associated with alterations in gut microbiota composition, including changes in the relative abundance of several bacterial taxa linked to inflammation and metabolic functions. However, whether these microbial changes play a causal role in the observed protection remains to be determined. These findings indicate that baicalin protects against endometritis through coordinated regulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis, and this protection was associated with shifts in gut microbiota composition. The results provide insight into the host-microbiota interactions accompanying endometritis and support baicalin as a potential therapeutic candidate, while highlighting the need for further causal investigations.

papers.title: Integrated endocrine-oxidative-metabolic and trace element responses to heat and cold stress in dromedary camels (Camelus dromedarius).
papers.authors: Zaki MG, Ramadan ES, Oraby MI, Ryad NM
papers.abstract: The dromedary camel (Camelus dromedarius) possesses remarkable physiological adaptations to withstand harsh desert conditions, including heat stress and drought. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of heat and cold stress on oxidative stress biomarkers, hormones, lipid, and mineral concentrations in dromedary camels. A total of 45 apparently healthy adult male dromedary camels were included in the study. Blood samples were collected, plasma and serum were separated for the determination of oxidative stress biomarkers, hormones, metabolic, and trace mineral parameters. During heat stress, cortisol, zinc, and copper concentrations increased significantly (p < 0.05), whereas total antioxidant capacity (TAC), triiodothyronine (T3), glucose, and triglyceride concentrations decreased significantly (p < 0.05). In contrast, cold stress was associated with significant (p < 0.05) increases in catalase (CAT), malondialdehyde (MDA), T3, glucose, and cortisol concentrations, while TAC, triglycerides, and copper concentrations decreased significantly (p < 0.05). Strong positive (p < 0.01) correlation between T3 and thyroxine (T4), whereas a strong negative (p < 0.01) correlation was observed between zinc and cholesterol. Positive (p < 0.05) correlations were also detected between glucose and MDA, cortisol and CAT, and copper and TAC. Conversely, negative (p < 0.05) correlations were found between triglycerides and CAT, triglycerides and T4, triglycerides and cortisol, zinc and triglycerides, cholesterol and glucose, and copper and MDA. During summer, positive correlations were observed between glucose and MDA, T3 and T4, as well as between cholesterol and both T3 and T4. In contrast, glucose showed negative correlations with both T3 and T4, while zinc was negatively correlated with copper. During autumn, positive correlations were detected between CAT and TAC, T3 and T4, and glucose and zinc. Conversely, negative correlations were observed between triglycerides and TAC, cortisol and T4, glucose and cholesterol, and zinc and cholesterol. During winter, T3 was positively correlated with zinc but negatively correlated with TAC. Cold stress exerted a more pronounced effect on oxidative balance and metabolic activity in dromedary camels than heat stress. Regular monitoring of these parameters is recommended for the early detection of physiological disturbances during the cold season.

papers.title: Suspected recurrent sarcoma resembling feline injection-site sarcoma with spinal cord invasion in a cat.
papers.authors: Pope EA, Cox A, Premanandan C, Selting KA, Selmic LE
papers.abstract: A 6-year-old, neutered male domestic shorthair cat was referred for evaluation of a recurrent subcutaneous mass on the right caudodorsolateral hip, 4 months after excision of a presumed feline injection site sarcoma (FISS). Advanced imaging revealed a bilobed soft tissue mass closely associated with the sciatic nerve and rectum. Surgical excision was limited by adjacent structures, and histopathology confirmed a sarcoma with incomplete margins. Definitive-intent radiation therapy was administered postoperatively. Follow-up imaging initially demonstrated no evidence of local recurrence. Approximately 9 months after completion of radiation therapy, the cat developed progressive pelvic limb paraparesis, fecal incontinence and urinary retention. MRI identified a large contrast-enhancing extradural spinal lesion extending from L5 to the sacrum, with suspected intramedullary invasion and marked thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots. Surgical exploration with hemilaminectomy and spinal cord biopsy revealed a poorly differentiated sarcoma histologically similar to the original tumor. Progressive disease was confirmed on follow-up imaging, and palliative radiation therapy was administered. Despite treatment, the cat developed severe neurologic deterioration and was humanely euthanized. This report describes the first documented case of spinal cord invasion secondary to a FISS-like fibrosarcoma without local recurrence at the primary site. Perineural invasion along the sciatic nerve is proposed as a biologically plausible mechanism of tumor extension. This case highlights an uncommon but severe pattern of disease progression and underscores the importance of considering perineural spread in incompletely excised FISS-like tumors associated with major peripheral nerves. Recurrent tumor affecting the spinal cord in a cat Injection site sarcomas are aggressive cancers in cats that can develop at sites of previous injections or inflammation. These tumors often grow quickly and can be difficult to fully remove with surgery, especially when they are located near important structures such as nerves or organs. In this case, a 6-year-old cat developed a cancerous mass on his right hip that recurred shortly after initial surgery. Because the tumor was close to the sciatic nerve and rectum, complete removal with wide margins was not possible. Radiation therapy was used to help control the disease, and imaging initially suggested the cancer was stable. Several months later, the cat began showing signs of nerve damage, including weakness in the back legs, difficulty jumping, and loss of bowel and bladder control. Advanced imaging of the spine revealed a new mass compressing and invading the spinal cord. Surgery and biopsy confirmed that this lesion was also cancerous and likely related to the original tumor. Despite additional radiation treatment, the cancer progressed, leading to severe neurologic decline. The cat was ultimately euthanized for quality-of-life reasons. This case is important because it documents a previously unreported complication of injection site sarcoma: spread of the tumor into the spinal cord. The findings suggest that cancer cells may travel along nerves, even when no mass is visible at the original surgery site. Greater awareness of this potential behavior may help veterinarians better monitor and manage cats with aggressive sarcomas, particularly when tumors are located near major nerves.

papers.title: Sero-epidemiological survey of Toxoplasma gondii in water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) and domestic pig (Sus scrofa domesticus) across upper and lower Egypt.
papers.authors: Elmahallawy EK, Abdo W, Cano-Terriza D, Gareh A, Elsheikh HEM, AlGabbani Q, Elaref MY, Fajardo-Alonso T, Soliman SS, Villena I, Salama MS, El-Khadragy MF, Sadek SAS, Shukry M, Almería S, García-Bocanegra I
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii (T. gondii) is a globally prevalent protozoan parasite affecting warm-blooded species, including humans. In Egypt, serological surveys have been conducted in several livestock; however, studies on species such as buffalo and pigs remain scarce. This study aimed to provide updated insights into the seroprevalence of T. gondii in a cohort of 548 domestic animals, comprising 288 water buffaloes (Bubalus bubalis), sampled from both Upper and Lower Egypt, and 260 domestic pigs (Sus scrofa domesticus) from Lower Egypt between January and December 2023. Serological screening for anti-T. gondii antibodies was performed using the Modified Agglutination Test (MAT). Furthermore, the investigation evaluated the influence of various individual factors, including sex, age, season, and geographic origin, on the likelihood of exposure to the parasite in these understudied host species. Likewise, this work comprehensively reviews all previous research on the serosurveys of T. gondii in water buffalo and domestic pigs across Upper and Lower Egypt, with findings systematically tabulated to provide an updated and consolidated overview of the available evidence about this topic. The overall seroprevalence of T. gondii in buffalo was 42.01% (121/288; 95% Confidence Interval (95%CI): 36.31- 47.71). The Generalized Estimating Equation model identified geographic location as a significant risk factor for T. gondii exposure in buffalo, where buffalo from Lower Egypt showing 3.69-fold higher odds of seropositivity compared to those from Upper Egypt, highlighting increased circulation of the parasite in northern areas. Seroprevalence was significantly higher in pigs (68.46%; 178/260; 95%CI: 62.81-74.11) than in buffalo. However, no significant associations were found between seropositivity and the evaluated epidemiological variables in this species. These findings demonstrate high T. gondii exposure in Egyptian buffalo and pigs, indicating continued transmission and zoonotic danger. Biosecurity measures must be strengthened, cat access reduced, sanitation enhanced, herd screening performed on a regular basis, and farmers educated. One Health surveillance and additional field research should lead effective control and lessen the public health effects. reveal substantial exposure to T. gondii in both buffalo and pigs in Egypt and highlight the need for targeted control strategies, including improved husbandry and biosecurity practices, routine animal screening, and farmer education, to reduce transmission risk in livestock and protect public health.

papers.title: Effect of 24-hour sedation during mechanical ventilation on hematological, biochemical, and coagulation parameters in bitches: A randomized clinical study.
papers.authors: Regalin D, Adorno BA, Chimenes ND, Ribeiro D, de Moraes RS, Benevenuto LGD, Serighelli-Júnior G, Saito ME, Comassetto F, Regalin BDDC, Padilha VS, Volpato J, Oleskovicz N
papers.abstract: The effects of prolonged sedation on hematological, biochemical, and coagulation variables have not been previously investigated in veterinary medicine. Twelve healthy adult mixed-breed female dogs were included. Blood samples (6 mL) were collected at baseline (M0) for complete blood count (CBC), biochemical testing, prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (PTT) and fibrinogen. After M0, dogs were allocated into two groups: midazolam-fentanyl-propofol group (MFG; n = 6), which received a continuous infusion of midazolam (0.5 mg/kg/h), fentanyl (10 µg/kg/h), and propofol (18 mg/kg/h); and ketamine-morphine-propofol group (KMG; n = 6), which received a continuous infusion of ketamine (0.6 mg/kg/h), morphine (0.26 mg/kg/h), and propofol (18 mg/kg/h). The infusion was maintained for 24 hours under mechanical ventilation. Laboratory parameters were reassessed from 12 to 24 hours after the beginning of infusion (M12 and M24), and at 12, 24, and 48 hours after the infusion (T12, T24, and T48). Both protocols significantly reduced erythrocyte count, packed cell volume, and haemoglobin concentration. In KMG, TTP decreased significantly at M12, M24, and T24; TSP at M24; and lymphocytes at M12 and M24. No significant changes were observed in ALP, ALT, albumin, globulins, creatinine, urea, glucose and blood coagulation. Triglyceride and cholesterol concentrations increased significantly from M6 to T48, but without biochemical evidence of hepatic, renal, or coagulation impairment. Overall, both protocols induced transient hematological and biochemical changes without clinically meaningful alterations in hepatic or renal function, supporting their use in healthy dogs mechanically ventilated for 24 hours.

papers.title: Simply adding positive end-expiratory pressure has limited effects on oxygenation in obese dogs.
papers.authors: Martin-Flores M, Araos J, Rondon TA
papers.abstract: Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) can be used to prevent atelectasis during anesthesia. We evaluated the effect of PEEP on intra- and postoperative oxygenation on obese dogs admitted for stifle surgery. Dogs received no PEEP (ZEEP; n = 10) or 7 cmH 2 O PEEP (n = 9) at random during general anesthesia. The partial pressure of arterial oxygen (PaO 2 ) and its ratio to inspired fractional oxygen (PaO 2 :FiO 2 ) were measured at start and end of surgery (FiO 2 1.0), and 20, 120, and 240 minutes after extubation (FiO 2 0.2). Cases of hypoxemia (PaO 2 < 80 mmHg) were identified. There were no differences between treatment for either variable (P > 0.1 for treatment and P > 0.6 for treatment*time, for both variables). There were three cases of postoperative hypoxemia in the ZEEP treatment (P = 0.21). No significant improvement was achieved when PEEP 7 cmH 2 O was applied in isolation. Successful use of PEEP may require additional maneuvers.

papers.title: Electrochemotherapy with carboplatin and bleomycin associated with mastectomy in cats with mammary carcinoma: A pilot study.
papers.authors: Regadas R, Dias GS, Brunner CHM, Carvalho VMP, Silva LP, Damasceno KA, Fontes TN, Rocha MAN, Barrouin-Melo SM, Machado MCA, Estrela-Lima A
papers.abstract: In cats, the high incidence of malignant mammary neoplasms with elevated rates of metastasis and recurrence underscores the need for more effective therapies to prevent disease progression. This preliminary study evaluated the impact of carboplatin or bleomycin electrochemotherapy on recurrence rates, adverse effects, and overall survival in female cats with mammary carcinoma undergoing mastectomy. Thirty-four female cats with mammary carcinoma were assigned to four groups: Group 1 (mastectomy), Group 2 (mastectomy plus chemotherapy), Group 3 (mastectomy plus electrochemotherapy with carboplatin and chemotherapy), and Group 4 (mastectomy plus electrochemotherapy with bleomycin and chemotherapy). The tumors were classified and graded histologically, and the proliferative index was assessed using Ki-67. Most cases were stage III, and 50% had nodal metastases. The predominant tumor types included cribriform carcinoma and histological grade II. All groups showed a high Ki-67 proliferation index (>20%), with no significant differences (p = 0.753). Hematocrit values in the fourth chemotherapy session were higher in G3 than in G2 (p = 0.022). The highest numerical recurrence rate occurred in G1, while no recurrences were observed in G2 or G4 during follow-up; however, this difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.086). Overall survival analysis showed a 82% mortality rate; G1 had 100% mortality, with a significant difference compared with the other groups (p = 0.0287). More chemotherapy sessions (≥5) were significantly associated with increased overall survival (p = 0.002), adding a mean of 39.1 days to disease-free survival per additional session. Taken together, these preliminary findings suggest that mastectomy alone was insufficient to control progression the cancer. Carboplatin-based protocols, whether used as conventional chemotherapy or combined with electrochemotherapy, showed lower recurrence rates, fewer adverse effects, and longer overall survival. However, due to the limited sample size, these results should be interpreted with caution. Further studies with larger cohorts are warranted to confirm these observations.

papers.title: Giant mammary fibroadenoma in four female dogs.
papers.authors: Dos Reys MP, de Sousa CG, Santana TCF, Nakagaki KYR, Cassali GD
papers.abstract: Fibroadenoma is a benign neoplasm with high prevalence in women but is rare in dogs. Its giant variant is defined by the lesion's size (exceeding 5 cm) and weight. The standard treatment is surgical excision. The objective of this study was to demonstrate that the subclassification of giant fibroadenoma, as described in humans, can also be observed in female dogs, as evidenced by four cases analyzed. The evaluation comprised macroscopic examination and histopathological analysis, underscoring the importance of differential diagnosis and the characterization of this condition in the canine species.

papers.title: In vitro evaluation of temperature-dependent stability and antimicrobial activity of reconstituted cefovecin sodium.
papers.authors: Fukayama T, Iwahana M, Yamada H, Hamabe L
papers.abstract: Cefovecin sodium is a long-acting third-generation cephalosporin widely used in dogs and cats. After reconstitution, refrigerated storage for a limited period is recommended; however, experimental data regarding the effects of alternative controlled storage temperatures on drug stability and antimicrobial activity are limited. This study evaluated, under in vitro conditions, the impact of storage temperature on the physicochemical stability and antimicrobial activity of reconstituted cefovecin sodium. Samples were stored at room temperature (25 ± 2°C), refrigerated conditions (4°C), or frozen conditions (-20°C) for up to 12 weeks. Visual appearance, absorbance at 360 nm, minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) against E. coli and Staphylococcus aureus, and cefovecin sodium concentrations determined by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) were assessed over time. Room temperature storage resulted in progressive discoloration, increased absorbance, elevated MIC values, and a significant decrease in drug concentration at later time points. Refrigerated storage delayed these changes, although mild increases in absorbance and MIC values were descriptively observed at later time points. In contrast, frozen storage preserved physicochemical properties, antimicrobial activity, and measured drug concentrations throughout the study period. These findings demonstrate that storage temperature influences the stability and in vitro antimicrobial activity of reconstituted cefovecin sodium in a condition-dependent manner. The results provide experimental reference data under controlled laboratory conditions and do not support clinical use outside the manufacturer's approved storage instructions.

papers.title: A new era in the early treatment of dioctophymosis - The first laparoscopic nephrotomy without ischemia in a dog.
papers.authors: Caye P, Gasparotto JC, Hörbe AV, Socolhoski BVG, Paraguassú AO, Pozzobon FM, Reinstein RDS, Müller DCM, Brun MV
papers.abstract: The parasite Dioctophyme renale is a nematode that infects carnivores and often causes total and irreversible destruction of renal tissue. In cases of early diagnosis, nephrotomy is an alternative for renal preservation. This report describes the first laparoscopic nephrotomy performed without ischemia in the treatment of a female dog with renal dioctophymosis, using an ultrasonic scalpel for hemorrhage control. The technique stood out for its precision in simultaneous renal parenchyma incision and coagulation, eliminating the need for temporary blood flow interruption to the organ. It allowed the removal of a 32 cm D. renale from inside the kidney.
